title: Per-plan quotas (compilations / optimizations / history retention) are advertised and sold but never enforced anywhere in the backend
impact: Any user who registers (free plan, ₹0) gets unlimited LaTeX compilations and unlimited LLM optimizations billed to the platform OpenAI/Anthropic key, despite the free plan advertising 0 optimizations and 3 compilations. Basic subscribers (₹299) get Pro-level unlimited usage. The entire paid tier's value proposition (usage limits) is unenforced, so there is no reason to upgrade and LLM spend is unbounded per free account.
fix: Add a per-user, per-period usage meter (e.g. a Redis counter keyed `user:{id}:{period}:{metric}` or a SQL count over `compilations`/`optimizations`) checked against `get_plan_config(plan)["features"]` in `submit_job` and the other LLM entrypoints, returning 402/429 when exhausted; increment only on successful completion.
corr: Real defect, but severity is high rather than critical, and it is a monetization/cost-control gap, not a security issue. Accurate statement: per-plan usage quotas in SUBSCRIPTION_PLANS (compilations, optimizations, historyRetention) are surfaced to the UI via payment_service.get_user_subscription() but never enforced in the backend; for authenticated users the plan only affects Celery queue priority, displayed ETA, compile timeout (get_compile_timeout), and whether a client-chosen model is honoured. Device-trial enforcement in job_routes.submit_job is deliberately anonymous-only, so any registered free user can run unlimited compiles and unlimited LLM optimizations on the platform OpenAI/Anthropic key (orchestrator.py:103 falls back to settings.OPENAI_API_KEY). Abuse is not literally unbounded: the global RateLimitMiddleware caps 60 req/min and 1000 req/hour per derived client id (fail-open if Redis is unavailable), and the separate /v1 developer API does enforce per-plan daily caps fail-closed. historyRetention is unimplemented in both directions (no pruning job exists), so it is dead config rather than a bypassed limit.
evidence: Plans define hard limits: free = `"compilations": 3, "optimizations": 0, "historyRetention": 0`; basic = `50 / 10 / 30`; pro = `"unlimited"`. `grep -rn 'features\[|features.get|quota|monthly_limit|historyRetention'` over `backend/app` returns **zero** enforcement sites — the only consumers are `get_user_subscription()` (`"features": plan_config.get("features", {})`, returned to the UI) and `PricingCard`/`SubscriptionManager` which render them. In `submit_job` the resolved plan is used only for queue priority and ETA (`safe_model = request.model if resolve_plan_family(resolved_plan) in {"pro","byok","team"} else None`, `estimated_time = int(estimated_time * 0.7)`), and the trial check is explicitly skipped for authenticated users (`if user_id is None and request.job_type in _TRIAL_JOB_TYPES`). No per-user usage counter is ever incremented or compared against `features`.
repro: Register a new account (plan stays `free`), then POST `/api/v1/jobs/submit` with `job_type: "combined"` repeatedly with a valid session cookie. Every request is queued and consumes a platform LLM call; no 402/429 is ever returned and no counter is stored.

title: Compilation rows never leave status='processing' — silently breaks Feature 10 (share links), 87 (one-click apply), 88 (compile error history), 49 (bulk PDF export) and dashboard success-rate, all marked done
impact: A user compiles a resume, clicks Share, and gets 404 "No compiled PDF available yet. Please compile your resume first." — the P1 Feature 10 marked "✅ COMPLETED" never works. Same for Apply-to-Greenhouse/Lever (422), Compile Error History panel (always empty), Export-All-as-PDF ZIP (always empty), and /dashboard success rate + avg compile time (always 0). Weekly digest emails always report a null average ATS score.
fix: Reconcile the Compilation row where the job actually finishes: in `latex_worker.py` / `orchestrator.py` (or a small Celery task they enqueue) set status/compilation_time/pdf_size/pdf_path/ats_score on `job.completed`/`job.failed`, instead of relying on a `GET /jobs/{id}/result` call the UI never makes. Upload the PDF to MinIO and set `pdf_path` there rather than lazily in the share path.
corr: The core defect is real and correctly located, with two scoping refinements: (1) The anonymous-share path in routes.py (the branch before line ~1196) never consults the Compilation table — it resolves the PDF from MinIO key `shares/{resume_id}/anon.pdf` or `TEMP_DIR/{anon_job_id}/resume.pdf` — so anonymous share links still function; only the normal/authenticated share path (routes.py:1198-1213) is broken. (2) The reason no reconciliation happens is not merely that the frontend "never calls" GET /jobs/{job_id}/result for compile flows: the one place the frontend does call it (useFormatConversion.ts:53) is a `format_conversion` job, and job_routes.py:439 only creates Compilation rows for job_type in ("latex_compilation", "combined") — so that call can never reconcile anything either. Additionally, Compilation.pdf_path is never populated on create or on the reconcile path (only opportunistically inside the share endpoint's temp-dir fallback), so even a hypothetically "completed" row would depend on the TEMP_DIR fallback. Severity high/critical is justified: the fix belongs in the worker/event path (latex_worker or orchestrator on job.completed), not in a GET handler.
evidence: `job_routes.py:443` creates every record as `Compilation(user_id=..., job_id=job_id, status="processing", ...)`. The ONLY code in the whole backend that ever writes `Compilation.status` is inside `GET /jobs/{job_id}/result` (`job_routes.py:784`: `update(Compilation).where(Compilation.job_id == job_id, Compilation.status == "processing").values(status=final_status, compilation_time=..., pdf_size=...)`); `rg -n 'update\(Compilation\)|compilation\.status\s*='` over `backend/app` returns exactly that one hit, and no worker touches it. But the frontend never calls that endpoint for compile/optimize flows — `apiClient.getJobResult` (api-client.ts:977) has zero callers outside `api-client.ts`, and the only fetch of `/jobs/{id}/result` anywhere in the frontend is `src/hooks/useFormatConversion.ts:53` (the file-import flow). `useJobStream` consumes the `job.completed` WebSocket event and stops. `apiClient.trackCompilation(...)` (called from edit/optimize/try/cover-letter pages) routes to `analytics_service.track_compilation_event`, which only writes a `UsageAnalytics` row (`analytics_service.py:660-673`) and never touches the `Compilation` table. Consumers that therefore always miss: `routes.py:1198` share endpoint selects `Compilation.status == "completed"` then `raise HTTPException(404, "No compiled PDF available yet. Please compile your resume first.")`; `application_routes.py:126` `.where(Compilation.resume_id == resume_id, Compilation.status == "completed")` then 422 "No compiled PDF found for this resume"; `error_history_service.py:87` filters `Compilation.status == "failed"`; `analytics_service.py:116` `func.count(Compilation.id).filter(Compilation.status == "completed")`; `resume_routes.py:2005` bulk-export PDF path filters on `"completed"`. Relatedly `Compilation.ats_score` is read at `email_worker.py:163` but written nowhere.
repro: Log in, open /workspace/{id}/edit, compile successfully (PDF renders), then POST /resumes/{id}/share and GET /share/{token} → 404. Verify with `SELECT status FROM compilations` — every row is 'processing'.

title: BYOK page crashes with a TypeError: the /api/byok/api-keys proxy double-wraps the backend response
impact: Any signed-in user opening /byok gets a client-side exception instead of the API key manager; the entire BYOK page (the paid "bring your own key" feature) is unusable. `onKeysChange(keys)` also feeds the same object into `ProviderSelector`, whose `userApiKeys.some(...)` would throw too.
fix: Make the api-keys GET proxy a pass-through like providers/route.ts: `return NextResponse.json(data)`, or unwrap correctly with `api_keys: data.api_keys ?? [], total_count: data.total_count ?? 0`.
corr: The defect is real and the crash mechanism is exactly as described, but severity is high rather than critical: it breaks rendering of the /byok page for all signed-in users with no data loss, corruption, or security exposure. Scope is limited to the GET handler in frontend/src/app/api/byok/api-keys/route.ts (lines 19-24); the POST handler in the same file correctly spreads the backend payload. Fix is to pass the backend response through unchanged, as frontend/src/app/api/byok/providers/route.ts already does.
evidence: Backend `GET /byok/api-keys` has `response_model=UserAPIKeysResponse` = `{success: bool, api_keys: List[APIKeyInfo], total_count: int}`. The Next proxy then does: `const transformedData = { success: true, total_count: data.length || 0, api_keys: data || [] }` — `data` is the backend *object*, so `data.length` is `undefined` (→ total_count always 0) and `api_keys` is set to the whole object. The client reads `const keys = data.api_keys || []; setApiKeys(keys)` and renders `{apiKeys.length === 0 ? ... : apiKeys.map((key) => ...)}`. `apiKeys` is an object, so `.length` is `undefined` (`undefined === 0` is false) and `.map` throws. The sibling `providers/route.ts` gets this right with an explicit comment: "Backend already returns { success, providers: [...], total_count } — pass through".
repro: Sign in, add at least one BYOK key (or none), navigate to /byok. `fetch('/api/byok/api-keys')` returns `{success, total_count: 0, api_keys: {success, api_keys: [...], total_count: N}}` and `apiKeys.map` throws.

title: Production backend image listens on port 8000 while every consumer (nginx, healthchecks, k8s probes, Prometheus) targets 8030
loc: backend/Dockerfile.prod:63-70, nginx/nginx.conf:63, docker-compose.prod.yml:81, k8s/backend/deployment.yaml (containerPort/probes 8030 + Service targetPort 8030), monitoring/prometheus.yml:23
impact: A production deploy is a total outage: nginx returns 502 for every /api request, the compose healthcheck marks backend permanently unhealthy, k8s readiness never passes so the backend pods are never added to the Service (CrashLoop/NotReady forever), and Prometheus reports the backend down.
fix: Change backend/Dockerfile.prod to `EXPOSE 8030`, health-check 8030 and `CMD ["uvicorn","app.main:app","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","8030","--workers","4"]` (or better, honour $PORT via an entrypoint script).
corr: The port mismatch is real and breaks the docker-compose.prod.yml deployment path: nginx proxies /api/, /jobs/ws/ and the auth routes to backend:8030 while the Dockerfile.prod CMD hardcodes uvicorn on 8000, and the backend publishes no host ports, so all API/WS requests return 502 and Prometheus reports the backend down. Corrections to the stated impact: containers do start normally (uvicorn binds 8000 fine) and nothing gates on healthchecks (no depends_on: condition: service_healthy), so the compose backend is merely permanently 'unhealthy' rather than restarting; k8s pods would be NotReady, not CrashLoopBackOff; and k8s/backend/deployment.yaml still references the placeholder image ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-backend:latest, so the k8s manifests are not an active deploy target. Fix: use 8030 (or shell-form --port ${PORT:-8030}) in Dockerfile.prod's CMD, EXPOSE and HEALTHCHECK.
evidence: backend/Dockerfile.prod ends with `HEALTHCHECK ... CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health`, `EXPOSE 8000`, `CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "4"]`. nginx/nginx.conf has `upstream backend { server backend:8030 ...}`; docker-compose.prod.yml backend healthcheck is `curl -f http://localhost:8030/health`; k8s/backend/deployment.yaml declares `containerPort: 8030` with liveness/readiness `httpGet: path: /health port: 8030`; monitoring/prometheus.yml scrapes `targets: ['backend:8030']`. PORT=8030 in the env is irrelevant because the CMD hardcodes --port 8000.
repro: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up --build, then curl -k https://localhost/api/health → 502; or `kubectl apply -f k8s/backend/deployment.yaml` → pods never Ready.

title: Production sets FASTAPI_ENV, which no code reads — ENVIRONMENT stays "development", disabling all prod hardening (public /docs, localhost CORS with credentials, skipped secret checks)
impact: In production: /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are publicly enumerable; CORS_ORIGINS keeps the default http://localhost:3000/5180-5183 entries with allow_credentials=True, so any page a victim loads on localhost can make credentialed cross-origin calls to the prod API; and the guardrails that reject placeholder/weak BETTER_AUTH_SECRET/JWT_SECRET_KEY and require a valid API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY are silently skipped.
fix: Add `ENVIRONMENT=production` to docker-compose.prod.yml (backend, worker, beat) and to k8s/backend/deployment.yaml (it already exists as latexy-config key `environment`), and delete the unused FASTAPI_ENV entries.
corr: Real defect, severity high rather than critical. Production manifests set FASTAPI_ENV=production, which no backend code reads, so settings.ENVIRONMENT stays "development" and is_production_like() is False in production. Confirmed consequences: /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are publicly served (main.py:99); CORS keeps the default http://localhost:3000 and 5180-5183 (+127.0.0.1) origins with allow_credentials=True (config.py:61-75, 456-462, main.py:118-124); the API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY presence requirement (config.py:493) and the placeholder/weak BETTER_AUTH_SECRET/JWT_SECRET_KEY rejection (config.py:503-518) are skipped; and the _check_cors_origins_on_startup warning (api/routes.py:203-213) is itself gated on is_production_like() so it never fires. Corrections to the report: (1) the localhost CORS risk requires the attacker to control an origin on the victim's own localhost dev ports, not any arbitrary page; (2) the Fernet validity check for API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unconditional and still runs, so only the presence requirement is lost; (3) docker-compose.prod.yml's backend/worker env lists also omit BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and JWT_SECRET_KEY, which are unconditionally required, so that compose file cannot boot at all — the reachable misconfigured path is k8s/backend/deployment.yaml, which injects all secrets but no ENVIRONMENT or CORS_ORIGINS. Fix: set ENVIRONMENT=production (and CORS_ORIGINS) in docker-compose.prod.yml, k8s/backend/deployment.yaml, and .env.production, or have config.py fall back to FASTAPI_ENV/DEPLOY_ENV via a validation_alias.
evidence: `rg FASTAPI_ENV` matches only docker-compose.prod.yml and k8s/backend/deployment.yaml — zero matches in backend/. config.py declares `ENVIRONMENT: str = "development"` and `is_production_like()` returns True only for {"production","staging"}. main.py: `_docs_enabled = not settings.is_production_like()`. config.py `effective_cors_origins()` strips localhost only `if self.is_production_like()`, and the placeholder/short-secret rejection plus the `API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` requirement are both inside `if self.is_production_like()`. Neither prod compose, .env.production (key list contains FASTAPI_ENV and DEPLOY_ENV but no ENVIRONMENT), nor the k8s manifests set ENVIRONMENT.
repro: static-only: grep shows no producer of ENVIRONMENT in any prod manifest; the code paths above are unconditional on that value.

title: docker-compose.prod.yml never passes BETTER_AUTH_SECRET or JWT_SECRET_KEY, which Settings requires at import time
impact: Every backend/worker/beat container in the production compose stack raises ValueError while importing app.core.config and exits immediately — the stack cannot start at all.
fix: Add `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET}`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY=${JWT_SECRET_KEY}`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `FRONTEND_URL` to the backend/celery-worker/celery-beat env blocks (or attach `env_file: .env.production`).
corr: The defect is real but scoped to the docker-compose.prod.yml / scripts/deploy/deploy.sh (and .github/workflows/release.yml) deployment path, not all production deployments — the Kubernetes manifests at k8s/backend/deployment.yaml:67,72 correctly inject BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and JWT_SECRET_KEY from the latexy-secrets secret. Within the compose path the impact is as claimed: backend, celery-worker, and celery-beat raise ValueError at import of app.core.config (settings = Settings() at config.py:574) and crash-loop under restart: unless-stopped. Additionally, adding the two variables to the compose environment blocks is not sufficient on its own: root .env.production:71 only carries a placeholder BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=your_better_auth_secret_key and defines no JWT_SECRET_KEY, so the env template must be filled in too. Also worth noting backend/.dockerignore ignores env/ but not .env, so a developer with a local backend/.env can accidentally bake secrets into the prod image and mask this failure during local builds.
evidence: config.py model_post_init: `if not self.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: missing.append(...)`, `if not self.JWT_SECRET_KEY: missing.append(...)`, then `raise ValueError(f"Missing required environment variables: ...")` unless SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true. The backend and celery-worker environment blocks in docker-compose.prod.yml list DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, RAZORPAY_*, API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, OTEL_* — no BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, no JWT_SECRET_KEY, no env_file, and backend/Dockerfile.prod does not ship a .env.
repro: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up backend → ValueError: Missing required environment variables: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, JWT_SECRET_KEY.

title: nginx proxies the frontend to port 5180 but the production frontend container serves on 3000
loc: nginx/nginx.conf:70; frontend/Dockerfile.prod (EXPOSE 3000 / CMD node server.js); docker-compose.prod.yml:25-40
impact: Every non-/api request through nginx (i.e. the whole site) returns 502 in the compose production stack. The two files also disagree with each other, so whichever is 'right' the other is broken.
fix: Either set `PORT=5180` on the frontend service (and fix its healthcheck) or change the nginx upstream to `server frontend:3000;`. Pick one port and use it in nginx.conf, both Dockerfiles and the k8s frontend deployment/Service.
corr: docker-compose.prod.yml's frontend service omits PORT, so the Next standalone server listens on 3000 while nginx.conf's frontend upstream dials frontend:5180 — requests routed to the frontend upstream (`location /` and `/_next/static/`) would 502 in the compose prod stack. nginx.conf itself is consistent with k8s/frontend/deployment.yaml, which sets PORT=5180 explicitly; the defect is confined to docker-compose.prod.yml (plus stale EXPOSE 3000 and 3000-based healthchecks, and a nonexistent /health route in the frontend app). Backend-routed locations (/api/, /jobs/ws/, /auth*) are unaffected, and the same compose stack has a prior blocker (missing nginx/ssl certs required by nginx.conf), so this is a broken unmaintained deployment artifact — high/medium, not critical. Fix: add `- PORT=5180` to the frontend env in docker-compose.prod.yml and align EXPOSE/healthchecks.
evidence: nginx.conf: `upstream frontend { least_conn; server frontend:5180 ...}`. frontend/Dockerfile.prod: `HEALTHCHECK ... http://localhost:3000/health`, `EXPOSE 3000`, `CMD ["node", "server.js"]` — Next standalone defaults to PORT=3000, and docker-compose.prod.yml's frontend service sets only NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL and NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED (no PORT), while its healthcheck checks 3000.
repro: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up --build && curl -k https://localhost/ → 502 Bad Gateway.

title: Production WebSocket URL is wrong by construction: released frontend connects to /ws/ws/jobs, nginx proxies /jobs/ws/ (compose) — real backend route is /ws/jobs
loc: frontend/Dockerfile.prod (ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL=/ws), .github/workflows/release.yml (build-args NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL=/ws), frontend/src/lib/api-client.ts:3134-3139, nginx/nginx.conf:125-135, k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml (location /ws/), backend/app/api/ws_routes.py:56
impact: All real-time job progress (compile/LLM/ATS streaming) is dead in production: the WebSocket handshake fails and the UI falls back to whatever polling exists, or hangs on 'connecting'. The nginx /jobs/ws/ block is dead configuration.
fix: Build the frontend with `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL=` empty (so it derives ws://host + /ws/jobs) or make getWebSocketUrl not append when the base already ends in /ws; and give both nginx configs a `location /ws/ { proxy_pass http://backend; ... }` block with Upgrade/Connection headers. Delete the /jobs/ws/ block.
corr: Core claim confirmed. Refined: in production builds (frontend/Dockerfile.prod ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL=/ws, also passed by .github/workflows/release.yml and inherited by docker-compose.prod.yml), next.config.js bakes "/ws" into the bundle, so getWebSocketUrl() returns the root-relative "/ws/ws/jobs". ws-client.ts:138 `new URL(getWebSocketUrl())` throws TypeError on a relative URL, is swallowed by the catch at line ~180, and enters a permanent reconnect loop — so no handshake is even attempted (not just a 404). Even if an absolute base were used, /ws/ws/jobs is wrong: the backend serves only /ws/jobs (prefix-less ws_router, routes.py:45, main.py:151); nginx/nginx.conf's `location /jobs/ws/` is dead config and k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml's `location /ws/` forwards the doubled path. There is no polling fallback in useJobStream.ts, so all real-time progress is dead in these prod configurations. Local dev, docker-compose.yml, and CI are unaffected (absolute ws://localhost:PORT). Fix: either set the build-time base to "" (client requests /ws/jobs) or stop appending "/ws" in getWebSocketUrl, and add a /ws/ upgrade block to nginx/nginx.conf while removing the /jobs/ws/ block.
evidence: api-client.ts: `export function getWebSocketUrl() { const base = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL ?? (API_BASE.replace(/^http/,'ws')); return `${base}/ws/jobs` }`. The published image is built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL=/ws` (Dockerfile.prod ARG and release.yml build-args), so the URL becomes `/ws/ws/jobs`. The backend route is `@ws_router.websocket("/ws/jobs")` on a prefix-less router. nginx/nginx.conf only has `location /jobs/ws/ { proxy_pass http://backend/jobs/ws/; }` — a path no backend route serves — so /ws/... falls through to `location /` (the Next.js app). k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml has `location /ws/ { proxy_pass http://backend; }`, which forwards the doubled path /ws/ws/jobs → 404.
repro: static-only: compare the built NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL, getWebSocketUrl()'s appended '/ws/jobs', the nginx location blocks and ws_routes.py's registered path.

title: k8s nginx does not strip the /api prefix, so every API call from the production frontend build 404s
loc: k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml (location /api/ { proxy_pass http://backend; }), nginx/nginx.conf:111, frontend/Dockerfile.prod (ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api), frontend/src/lib/api-client.ts:9-10, backend/app/api/job_routes.py:64, backend/app/api/resume_routes.py:31
impact: On Kubernetes every REST call from the app returns 404: no resume list, no compile, no downloads. The bug is invisible in compose because that config happens to strip correctly.
fix: Change the k8s nginx ConfigMap to `proxy_pass http://backend/;` (and the /health, /compile, /flower blocks accordingly), or give the FastAPI routers a shared /api prefix and use it consistently.
corr: Real but low-severity/latent: k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml's `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://backend; }` omits the trailing slash and therefore does not strip the `/api` prefix, while nginx/nginx.conf:111 uses `proxy_pass http://backend/;` and does strip it — the two configs are inconsistent and the k8s one would 404 against the un-prefixed FastAPI routers. However this is not a production outage: the shipped prod stack (docker-compose.prod.yml) uses nginx/nginx.conf, and the k8s manifests are unused placeholder templates (image `ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-frontend:latest`, empty registry secret, `YOUR_*` placeholder secrets, no CI/CD that applies them, and `api-url: http://nginx-service/api` / `ws-url: ws://nginx-service/ws` which are browser-unresolvable and mismatched with the real `/jobs/ws/` route). Fix is worthwhile hygiene (add the trailing slash, or add `location /api/ { rewrite }`) plus fixing the placeholder configmap URLs before anyone actually deploys to k8s.
evidence: The released frontend is built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api` and api-client builds URLs like `${API_BASE}/jobs/${id}`, `${API_BASE}/resumes/...`, `${API_BASE}/download/...`. Backend routers are `APIRouter(prefix="/jobs")`, `APIRouter(prefix="/resumes")` (only public_api_routes.py uses prefix="/api/v1"). k8s/nginx/nginx.yaml uses `proxy_pass http://backend;` (no trailing slash) so the request arrives as /api/jobs/... — which does not exist. nginx/nginx.conf uses `proxy_pass http://backend/;` (trailing slash) and does strip it, so the two prod proxies are mutually inconsistent.
repro: static-only: `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://backend; }` preserves the URI; backend has no /api/jobs route.

title: AI "optimize & compile" produces a PDF that is immediately deleted and never cached — download/preview/logs/SyncTeX always 404
impact: Every AI optimize-and-compile run (the flagship paid feature, plus /jobs/batch, quick-tailor and fork flows that call `submit_optimize_and_compile`) reports success with an ATS score but the user never sees a PDF — the editor shows only `toast.error('Failed to load PDF preview')` and an empty preview pane. Download, compile logs, and editor↔PDF SyncTeX are all dead for these jobs. Share-link PDF upload (resume_routes.py:1719-1731) and bulk PDF export also find nothing.
fix: In `_run_latex_stage`, before the `finally` runs, cache the artifacts exactly as `latex_worker` does: `setex latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf` (base64), `:log`, `:synctex` with `_DEFAULT_TTL`; or better, have the orchestrator delegate to the shared `run_latex_subprocess` helper and add caching there once.
corr: Real defect, severity high rather than critical. orchestrator._run_latex_stage (backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:522-639) rmtree's the job dir in a finally block and never persists resume.pdf / resume.log / resume.synctex.gz to Redis (unlike latex_worker.py:382/415/437), yet job.completed still returns pdf_job_id=job_id. Consequently, for every AI optimize-and-compile job GET /download/{job_id}, /download/{job_id}/synctex and /logs/{job_id} return 404, so the editor's auto PDF preview fails with 'Failed to load PDF preview' and download/logs/SyncTeX are unavailable for that job id. Not total feature loss: the optimized LaTeX is still streamed and saved into the editor, and pressing Compile produces a working, cached PDF via latex_worker; the share-link MinIO upload path only breaks when the orchestrator job is the latest completed Compilation record. Fix: cache pdf/log/synctex bytes (or upload to storage) in _run_latex_stage before the rmtree, mirroring latex_worker.
evidence: `_run_latex_stage` ends with `finally: shutil.rmtree(job_dir, ignore_errors=True)` (line 639) and its success branch is only `return True, compilation_time, "", page_count` — it never writes the PDF anywhere. `grep 'latexy:job:.*:pdf' backend/app` shows the only writer is `latex_worker.py:415`; orchestrator.py contains zero occurrences of `setex`/`redis`/`base64`. Yet the orchestrator still advertises the artifact: `publish_event(job_id, "job.completed", {... "pdf_job_id": job_id ...})`. `GET /download/{job_id}` tries `r.get(f"latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf")` (miss) then `get_job_files(job_id)` → `settings.TEMP_DIR/job_id/resume.pdf` (rmtree'd) → `raise HTTPException(404, "PDF not found...")`. Same for `/logs/{job_id}` and `/download/{job_id}/synctex`.

title: AI summary cache key hashes only the first 500 chars of the resume → one user's generated summary is served to another user
impact: Two users who start from the same template (the normal case — the app ships a template gallery) and request summaries with the same target_role collide on one cache entry. User B's SummaryGeneratorWidget renders professional summaries synthesised from user A's employment history/achievements: cross-tenant PII disclosure, and user B gets a summary that does not describe them.
fix: Hash the full resume_latex (and full job_description) with sha256, and namespace the key with the caller identity (`ai:summary:{user_id or 'anon'}:{digest}`) — mirror what _translate_cache_key already does.
corr: The defect is real but "critical" overstates it; it is high severity. Trigger conditions are opportunistic rather than attacker-controlled: a second user must have byte-identical first 500 chars (i.e. an unmodified preamble of the same seeded template), identical trimmed target_role, identical first 200 chars of job_description, and hit within the 30-minute TTL (ttl=1800). What leaks is LLM-paraphrased summary text derived from another user's resume body (employer names, titles, achievements), not raw stored resume content, and no stored resume record is exposed. It is simultaneously a guaranteed correctness bug (a user's own edits below char 500 return stale summaries). Fix: hash the full resume_latex and full job_description and include the authenticated identity/resume id in the key, matching _translate_cache_key at ai_routes.py:1290.
evidence: def _summary_cache_key(...): raw = f"{resume_latex[:500]}|{(target_role or '').strip()}|{(job_description or '')[:200].strip()}|{count}"  → "ai:summary:" + sha256(raw)[:16]. The cache is the shared Redis `cache_manager`, with no user_id in the key. For every stock template in backend/app/data/templates/**, the first 500 characters are pure preamble (\documentclass … \titleformat/\setlist) — the first real \section starts after char 500. Verified: prefix = fullstack.tex[:500] plus two completely different bodies ("Alice Smith, Staff Eng at Stripe" vs "Bob Jones, Intern at Foo") both produce key ai:summary:5abde6cdb68ab391. Compare _translate_cache_key two hundred lines below, which explicitly hashes the *entire* content with the comment "Hash entire content to avoid collision from shared preambles" — the same bug was fixed there and missed here.
repro: User A: POST /ai/generate-summary with resume = template + A's experience, target_role empty. User B (any account, or anonymous via /try): POST /ai/generate-summary with the same template preamble + B's own experience, target_role empty → response has cached=true and contains A's summaries. TTL 1800s.

title: LaTeX runs unsandboxed: docker fallback silently degrades to local pdflatex, and even the docker path has no network/memory/cpu/pids/read-only limits
impact: Every resume compile executes TeX in the same process namespace as the Celery worker, which has DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, OPENAI/ANTHROPIC keys and API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY in its environment and `./backend` (including backend/.env) bind-mounted at /app. Any TeX primitive that reads files or (via a shell-escape bypass) spawns a process operates with full worker credentials; there is also no memory/CPU ceiling, so one document can OOM the worker.
fix: Pick one execution model and enforce it: either require the sandbox (raise/fail the job if `shutil.which("docker")` is None instead of silently falling back) and add `--network none --read-only --memory=512m --cpus=1 --pids-limit=64 --user 1001`, or run pdflatex locally under an explicit `-no-shell-escape` plus `openin_any=p/openout_any=p` texmf settings, a dedicated unprivileged uid, and rlimits.
corr: Real but mis-scoped and over-severe (high at most, arguably medium). Accurate claim: the `shutil.which("docker")` branch in /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/workers/latex_worker.py:272, /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:546 and /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/services/latex_service.py:250 is dead in the containerized deployment (no /var/run/docker.sock in any compose/k8s manifest), so LaTeX always runs as a local pdflatex subprocess inside the Celery worker container — that container, not a per-job sandbox, is the only isolation boundary, and there is no memory/pids ceiling. Mitigations the finding ignores: --shell-escape is never passed and is not in _ALLOWED_EXTRA_FLAGS (default restricted shell escape); latex_worker.py:209 calls latex_service.validate_latex_content, which rejects \write18/\openout/\openin/\input18 and absolute/traversal \input-family arguments; the process runs as non-root appuser; COMPILE_TIMEOUT bounds runtime; and secrets are env vars with no backend/.env on disk, so the "TeX reads worker credentials / RCE" impact is not demonstrated. The concrete gaps worth fixing are: (1) orchestrator._run_latex_stage and latex_service.run_latex_subprocess skip validate_latex_content entirely, (2) the regex guard is bypassable via macro-built paths, and (3) add --network none/--memory/--pids-limit on the docker path plus openin_any=p texmf hardening for the local path.
evidence: All three compile paths do `_use_docker = shutil.which("docker") is not None`, and the docker command is only `["docker", "run", "--rm", "-v", f"{job_dir}:/workspace", "-w", "/workspace", settings.LATEX_DOCKER_IMAGE, compiler, ...]` — no `--network none`, `--memory`, `--cpus`, `--pids-limit`, `--read-only`, `--user`, and no explicit `-no-shell-escape`. The else-branch runs `[compiler, "-interaction=nonstopmode", ...]` directly via `subprocess.Popen`. The worker image installs `texlive-latex-base/extra` (backend/Dockerfile:9-13) but the compose `worker` service mounts only `./backend:/app` plus temp volumes — no `/var/run/docker.sock` anywhere in docker-compose*.yml or k8s/, so `shutil.which("docker")` is None in production and every compile is a local pdflatex inside the worker container.
repro: static-only: `grep -rn 'docker.sock' docker-compose*.yml k8s/` returns nothing while backend/Dockerfile installs texlive, so the `else` (local pdflatex) branch is the one taken in the deployed worker.

title: LaTeX injection blacklist is trivially bypassable, giving arbitrary host file read exfiltrated through streamed compile logs
impact: A user can submit a resume containing `\@@input /app/.env` or `\input{\string/proc/self/environ}`; the file's contents are echoed into the pdflatex log, streamed over the WebSocket to the attacker, and also land in the PDF. That discloses DATABASE_URL, API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY (which decrypts every user's BYOK key), Razorpay and BETTER_AUTH secrets. `\write 18{...}` additionally reaches TeX's restricted shell-escape command set.
fix: Stop relying on a command blacklist: run the compiler with `-no-shell-escape` and a texmf.cnf setting `openin_any = p` / `openout_any = p` (paranoid — restricts reads to the job directory), inside a network-less container whose only mount is the job dir. Keep the regex as defence-in-depth only.
corr: Real defect, but scope it correctly: the blacklist in latex_service.py:25-40 is bypassable (verified: `\makeatletter\@@input /path`, `\csname input\endcsname{...}`, `\write 18{...}` with a space, `\openin1=...`), and because the prod worker image (backend/Dockerfile.prod) has texlive but no docker CLI, latex_worker.py compiles in-process, so an attacker gets arbitrary read of any file readable inside the worker container (application source under /app, container filesystem, /proc entries), exfiltrated through the streamed `log.line` events, the Redis-cached log served by /logs/{job_id}, and the output PDF. Corrections to the finding: (1) `\write 18` only invokes TeX's restricted shell-escape command set (kpsewhich/bibtex/repstopdf-style), not arbitrary command execution; (2) production secrets are injected as environment variables (docker-compose.prod.yml), there is no /app/.env, so disclosure of API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY / DATABASE_URL / Razorpay secrets is only possible via /proc/self/environ, which is a zero-length proc file and yields partial/unreliable output — likely but not guaranteed. Severity high rather than critical; correct fix is a texmf.cnf with openin_any=p/openout_any=p plus shell_escape=f (and ideally an isolated/read-only compile sandbox), not regex blacklisting.
evidence: The guards are `_SHELL_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?:write18|openout|openin|input18)\b")` and `_ABS_FILE_READ_RE` which requires the character immediately after the (optional) brace to be `/`, `~`, `..` or a drive letter. I verified against the exact patterns: `\write 18{id}` (a space is legal between `\write` and the stream number) → no match; `\input{\string/etc/passwd}` → no match; `\@@input /etc/passwd` (LaTeX kernel's saved `\input` primitive) → no match; `\csname input\endcsname{/etc/passwd}` → no match. TeX Live's default `openin_any=a` permits reading any readable file, and every pdflatex output line is broadcast to the user: `publish_event(job_id, "log.line", {"line": stripped, "source": compiler, ...})`, plus the full log is cached at `latexy:job:{job_id}:log` and served by `/logs/{job_id}`.
repro: POST /compile (or /jobs with type=latex_compilation) with a minimal document containing `\@@input /app/.env`, then read the `log.line` events / GET /logs/{job_id}.

title: Orchestrator deletes the compiled PDF before publishing job.completed — every AI optimize+compile download 404s
impact: Every "Optimize + Compile" run (workspace optimize page and the anonymous /try funnel) completes, streams the LaTeX, shows an ATS score, and then fails to render or download the PDF — frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/optimize/page.tsx:160 and src/app/try/page.tsx:89 both call `apiClient.downloadPdf(stream.pdfJobId)` and surface "Failed to load optimized PDF" / "Failed to load PDF preview". The Download PDF button (optimize/page.tsx:789, try/page.tsx:163) fails too.
fix: In `_run_latex_stage` (or the caller, before the finally), read `resume.pdf` and `resume.synctex(.gz)` and SETEX them to `latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf` / `:synctex` / `:log` exactly as latex_worker.py:388-424 does, or drop the unconditional rmtree and let cleanup_temp_files_task reclaim the directory.
corr: Confirmed with a severity nuance: the orchestrator's `_run_latex_stage` rmtree's `TEMP_DIR/{job_id}` in its `finally` and never caches the PDF/log/synctex bytes to Redis the way `latex_worker` does, so `GET /download/{job_id}` and `GET /logs/{job_id}` 404 for every combined (optimize+compile) job even though `job.completed` advertises `pdf_job_id`. Impact is limited to the PDF preview/download and compile logs of combined jobs — the streamed LaTeX, ATS score, changes list and auto-save checkpoint still succeed, and users can re-compile the returned LaTeX through the normal compile path — so this is a high-severity broken-feature bug rather than a total pipeline failure. Fix: read the PDF bytes (plus log text and synctex) before the rmtree in orchestrator.py:620-638 and `setex` them under `latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf` / `:log` / `:synctex`, mirroring latex_worker.py:379-440.
evidence: `_run_latex_stage` ends with `finally: shutil.rmtree(job_dir, ignore_errors=True)` and — unlike latex_worker, which does `get_worker_redis().setex(f"latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf", _DEFAULT_TTL, base64.b64encode(pdf_bytes)...)` — the orchestrator never caches the PDF bytes anywhere (grep for `:pdf` in orchestrator.py returns nothing). It still publishes `job.completed` with `"pdf_job_id": job_id`, and the module docstring claims "The job_id is used as the PDF storage path so GET /download/{job_id} serves the compiled PDF directly." `download_pdf` tries Redis key `latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf` (absent), then falls back to `settings.TEMP_DIR/{job_id}/resume.pdf` (rmtree'd) and raises 404. Same for `latexy:job:{job_id}:log`, which the orchestrator also never writes, so GET /logs/{job_id} 404s (routes.py:517).
repro: POST /jobs/submit with job_type="combined", wait for job.completed, then GET /download/{job_id} → 404 "PDF not found". Deterministic: rmtree runs synchronously before the ATS stage and before job.completed is published.

title: Anonymous share links are broken by construction and fall back to serving the UNREDACTED resume PDF
impact: A user who enables "anonymous" sharing (to hide name/email/phone via latex_pii_redactor) gets a link that, in the normal case, points at a MinIO key that is never written — visitors see a NoSuchKey XML error instead of the resume. In the MinIO-error case the endpoint instead hands the visitor a presigned URL to the full, unredacted PDF containing the exact PII the feature exists to strip.
fix: Use `storage_service.file_exists(anon_minio_key)` (already used by template_routes) before presigning, so the step-2 upload path is actually reachable; and when the redacted PDF is unavailable, return 404/202 with `anonymous_processing=true` instead of falling through to the unredacted `Compilation` branch. Also have the frontend honour `anonymous_processing`.
corr: Anonymous share links are broken by construction (medium severity, functional bug, not a PII leak). backend/app/api/routes.py:1160-1166 presigns shares/{resume.id}/anon.pdf without checking existence — generate_presigned_url (storage_service.py:79-86) is a local boto3 signing call that always returns a URL — so the `if not pdf_url and anon_job_id` block at routes.py:1168-1177 is dead code and is the only place in the repo that ever writes that key (the latex worker never uploads to MinIO). Result: every anonymous share link returns a presigned URL to a nonexistent object and visitors see a MinIO NoSuchKey XML error in the iframe (frontend/src/app/r/[token]/page.tsx:94); anonymous_processing is never read by the frontend, so there is no "still processing" UI either. The claimed fallback to serving the full unredacted PDF does NOT occur: any failure of _get_client()/presign is key-independent, so the normal-mode branch (routes.py:1216-1239) fails the same way and the request ends in a 404, never handing out the un-redacted PDF. Fix: gate on storage_service.file_exists(anon_minio_key) (or move the anon upload into the compile worker) and have the share page render a "preparing redacted copy" state when anonymous_processing is true.
evidence: In `get_shared_resume`: `anon_minio_key = f"shares/{resume.id}/anon.pdf"` then `pdf_url = generate_presigned_url(anon_minio_key, ttl=3600)` inside a try/except that only sets `pdf_url = None` on exception. `generate_presigned_url` is `client.generate_presigned_url("get_object", Params={...})` — boto3 signs a URL without checking object existence, so it always returns a non-empty string. Consequently the step-2 recovery block guarded by `if not pdf_url and anon_job_id:` (the ONLY code in the repo that ever calls `upload_bytes(anon_minio_key, ...)`) is unreachable dead code: `rg -n "anon.pdf" backend/app` matches only routes.py:1160 and routes.py:1170. When `_get_client()` does raise (MinIO misconfigured/unreachable), `pdf_url` becomes None, the code logs "Anonymous PDF not ready yet", sets `anonymous_processing = True` and FALLS THROUGH into the normal branch, which presigns the latest ordinary `Compilation.pdf_path` and returns it. The share page renders `<iframe src={data.pdf_url}` and never reads `anonymous_processing` (`rg -rn "anonymous_processing" frontend/src` matches only the type declaration in api-client.ts).
repro: POST /resumes/{id}/share with {"anonymous": true}, then GET /share/{share_token}. The returned pdf_url points at shares/{resume_id}/anon.pdf which nothing ever uploads. To see the leak, make storage_service._get_client() raise (e.g. MinIO down): the response returns the normal compilation PDF with is_anonymous=true.

title: POST /optimize and POST /optimize-and-compile are completely unauthenticated LLM endpoints on the platform API key
impact: Any anonymous internet caller can burn the operator's OpenAI/Anthropic budget at up to the generic IP rate limit (and unlimited if Redis is unavailable), with no trial counter, no plan check and no attribution. The synchronous compile variant also runs pdflatex per request.
fix: Add `user_id: Optional[str] = Depends(get_current_user_optional)` plus the same `trial_service.check_and_track_usage` gate used in job_routes.py:271, or delete both endpoints — no frontend code calls them (`rg "'/optimize" frontend/src/lib` returns nothing), so they are live-but-unused attack surface.
corr: Core defect confirmed as described. Two refinements: (1) the generic IP limiter also imposes RATE_LIMIT_CALLS_PER_HOUR (default 1000/hr) in addition to 60/min, keyed on session token or peer IP, so abuse while Redis is healthy is capped per-IP rather than unlimited — unlimited only during a Redis outage or via IP rotation; (2) both endpoints are dead legacy paths with no frontend or backend callers (the live path is POST /jobs/submit, which does enforce the anonymous trial), so the correct remediation is to delete them or attach the same `trial_service.check_and_track_usage` guard from backend/app/api/job_routes.py.
evidence: `@router.post("/optimize", response_model=OptimizationResponse)` / `async def optimize_resume(request: OptimizationRequest):` — the signature has no `Depends(get_current_user_optional)`, no `Depends(get_db)`, no device fingerprint, and the body calls `await llm_service.optimize_resume(request)` directly. `optimize_and_compile_resume` then calls `await optimize_resume(request)` plus `latex_service.compile_latex(...)`. Compare backend/app/api/job_routes.py:260-289, which explicitly enforces `trial_service.check_and_track_usage(...)` for anonymous callers, and backend/app/api/ai_routes.py:219-225, which routes anonymous callers through `_resolve_ai_api_key(db, user_id, client_ip)` specifically because "platform-key fallback is rate limited". Neither guard exists here. The only protection is the generic IP limiter (RATE_LIMIT_CALLS_PER_MINUTE, default 60) in backend/app/middleware/rate_limiting.py, which also fails open when Redis is down (`_warn_fail_open("rate limiting")`).
repro: curl -X POST http://localhost:8030/optimize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"latex_content":"\\documentclass{article}\\begin{document}x\\end{document}","job_description":"engineer"}' — no Authorization header, no X-Device-Fingerprint.

title: Collaboration WebSocket ignores the collaborator role — "viewer"/"commenter" get full write access to the document
impact: A resume owner who invites someone as "Viewer" (UI: "Read-only") or "Commenter" actually grants them full authority to rewrite the resume's Y.js document; edits persist and are relayed to everyone in the room. The permission label shown in the product is not enforced anywhere.
fix: Pass `collab.role` into the room's user_info and into `handle_collab_message`; drop SYNC_STEP2/MSG_UPDATE frames (allowing only awareness and SYNC_STEP1) for non-owner clients whose role is not "editor".
corr: The collaboration WebSocket does omit any role enforcement — /ws/collab/{resume_id} accepts any user with a ResumeCollaborator row regardless of role, and handle_collab_message persists and relays Y.js document updates from viewers/commenters exactly as from editors. But this is a medium-severity authenticated privilege escalation, not high: all REST resume endpoints are owner-only (GET/PUT /resumes/{id} filter on Resume.user_id), so a non-owner cannot open the editor UI and must hand-craft a raw WebSocket with lib0-encoded Y.js frames to exploit it; the writes land in a Redis CRDT log (24h TTL, 500-update cap) and only reach resumes.latex_content indirectly if the owner has the editor open and autosave fires. Fix: read collab.role, carry it in user_info, and pass it into handle_collab_message so SYNC_STEP2/MSG_UPDATE frames are dropped for viewer/commenter (awareness frames may still be relayed).
evidence: `collab_websocket` loads the `ResumeCollaborator` row (`collab = collab_result.scalar_one_or_none()`) and only checks `if collab is None: ... code=4003 Forbidden`. The row's `role` is never read; it is not put into `user_info` (only `is_owner`) and `handle_collab_message(resume_id, client_id, data, room)` has no role parameter — it dispatches SYNC_STEP2 / MSG_UPDATE frames straight to `room` persistence and peer relay. Roles are a real concept: `_VALID_ROLES = {"editor", "commenter", "viewer"}` (resume_routes.py:2048) and the UI advertises `viewer: { label: 'Viewer', desc: 'Read-only' }`.
repro: Owner: POST /resumes/{id}/collaborators {"email":"b@x.com","role":"viewer"}. As b@x.com connect to ws://host/ws/collab/{resume_id}?token=<session token> and send a Y.js MSG_UPDATE frame — it is persisted and broadcast.

title: Anonymous share links always return a presigned URL for a MinIO object that is never created — anonymous sharing is 100% broken
impact: Any user who enables anonymous sharing (`POST /resumes/{id}/share` with `{"anonymous": true}`) gets a share link whose PDF URL returns a MinIO `NoSuchKey` XML error forever. Because step 1 always "succeeds", the temp-dir fallback at routes.py:1170-1180 and the `anonymous_processing=True` flag (which the frontend uses to show a "still compiling" state) are unreachable dead code, so the user gets no error and no retry hint.
fix: Guard step 1 with `storage_service.file_exists(anon_minio_key)` before presigning (as template_routes.py already does), so the temp-dir fallback and `anonymous_processing` flag become reachable; and/or have latex_worker upload to `shares/{resume_id}/anon.pdf` when `metadata["anonymous_share"]` is set.
corr: The core defect is real: anonymous share links always return a presigned URL for `shares/{resume_id}/anon.pdf`, a key nothing ever writes, so the share page iframe shows a MinIO NoSuchKey error — anonymous sharing is fully broken, and both the temp-dir fallback and the anonymous_processing flag are dead code. Corrections: (a) `anonymous_processing` is not consumed by the frontend at all (only declared in api-client.ts:672), so no "still compiling" UI regressed; (b) more importantly, the obvious fix of guarding with storage_service.file_exists() would expose a worse bug — the fall-through at routes.py:1196+ returns the latest normal (unredacted) compilation's PDF with is_anonymous=True, leaking the PII the anonymous mode is meant to redact. A correct fix must persist the redacted PDF (worker-side upload, or Redis `latexy:job:{job_id}:pdf` lookup as in resume_routes.py:1723-1731) and return a processing/404 response rather than falling through.
evidence: `get_shared_resume` anonymous branch: `anon_minio_key = f"shares/{resume.id}/anon.pdf"` then `try: pdf_url = generate_presigned_url(anon_minio_key, ttl=3600) except Exception: pdf_url = None`. `generate_presigned_url` is `return client.generate_presigned_url("get_object", Params={...}, ExpiresIn=ttl)` — boto3 presigning is a pure local signing operation and never contacts the server, so it cannot raise for a missing key. Meanwhile `grep -rn 'anon.pdf' backend/app` finds exactly one hit (routes.py:1160) — nothing ever uploads to that key. The anon compile job is submitted with `metadata={"anonymous_share": True, ...}` (resume_routes.py:1758) and `grep -rn anonymous_share` shows the worker never reads it. Contrast template_routes.py:225/261 which correctly calls `storage_service.file_exists(...)` before downloading; `file_exists` exists in storage_service.py:67 and is not used here.
repro: POST /resumes/{id}/share with body {"anonymous": true}, then GET /share/{token}. Response contains pdf_url pointing at shares/{resume_id}/anon.pdf with is_anonymous=true and anonymous_processing=false; fetching that URL yields NoSuchKey.

title: Invited resume collaborators cannot load the resume — every REST resume endpoint is owner-only, so the collab editor 404s
impact: `POST /resumes/{id}/collaborators` succeeds and the CollaboratorPanel shows the invitee, but the invitee gets 404 from GET /resumes/{id}, the resume never appears in their /resumes list, and the editor page never loads — so Y.js collaboration is never reached. evidence: `GET /resumes/{resume_id}` filters `select(Resume, ...).where(Resume.id == resume_id, Resume.user_id == user_id)` and raises 404 if no row. `list_resumes` filters `Resume.user_id == user_id`. `grep -rn ResumeCollaborator backend/app` shows the table is consulted for authorization in exactly one place — the `/ws/collab/{resume_id}` WebSocket (ws_routes.py:302-311) — and nowhere in any REST handler. The editor page fetches content via `const data = await apiClient.getResume(resumeId)` (edit/page.tsx:1000) and only then, at line 2309, enables `collabEnabled`. Line 1044's `setCollabIsOwner(data.user_id === sessionUserId)` proves non-owners were meant to reach this page.
repro: As user A, POST /resumes/{id}/collaborators {"email":"b@x.com","role":"editor"} (201). As user B, GET /resumes/{id} → 404 "Resume not found"; navigating to /workspace/{id}/edit shows the load error.

title: Collaborator `role` (viewer / commenter) is stored and validated but never enforced — read-only collaborators get full write access
impact: A collaborator invited as `viewer` or `commenter` can, over the collab WebSocket, apply arbitrary Y.js updates to the shared document (which are persisted by collab_manager and relayed to all peers). The role selector in CollaboratorPanel.tsx is purely cosmetic — there is no read-only mode.
fix: Read `collab.role` in the permission block, put it in `user_info`, and in `handle_collab_message` reject `SYNC_STEP2` / `MSG_UPDATE` frames (allow only SYNC_STEP1 and awareness) for non-`editor` roles.
corr: Collaborator `role` is validated and persisted (resume_routes.py:2048 `_VALID_ROLES`, invite/PATCH endpoints) but never enforced on the collaboration WebSocket: ws_routes.py:296-311 only checks that a ResumeCollaborator row exists, and handle_collab_message (collab_manager.py:205-260) persists and relays SYNC_STEP2/MSG_UPDATE frames from any connected client. A user invited as `viewer` or `commenter` can therefore apply arbitrary Y.js updates to the shared CRDT document in Redis and have them broadcast to all peers. Scope is narrower than "full write access": non-owner collaborators are still blocked from every REST resume mutation by `_verify_resume_ownership`, so the injected content only becomes persisted resume content once a write-capable session (normally the owner) saves the merged document, and the attacker must already have been explicitly invited by the owner. Realistic severity: medium (integrity gap / role UI is misleading rather than a remote unauthenticated write).
evidence: ws_routes.py fetches the row (`collab = collab_result.scalar_one_or_none()`) and only checks `if collab is None: ... 4003 Forbidden` — `collab.role` is never read. The `user_info` dict built at ws_routes.py:317-323 carries `is_owner` but no role. `grep -n role backend/app/services/collab_manager.py` returns nothing, and `handle_collab_message` persists and relays `SYNC_STEP2 / MSG_UPDATE` frames from any connected client with no permission gate.

title: `Compilation.ats_score` does not exist on the model — the weekly digest email task always fails and is silently swallowed
impact: Every user who opts in via `PUT /settings/notifications {"weekly_digest": true}` never receives a digest. The failure is invisible outside worker logs — the fan-out task reports success because each per-user task swallows its own AttributeError.
fix: Compute avg ATS from `ATSScore` (the model that actually stores scores) joined to the user/resume, or drop the avg_ats column from the digest and pass None to `render_weekly_digest_email`.
corr: Real defect, but severity is medium rather than high. `func.avg(Compilation.ats_score)` at backend/app/workers/email_worker.py:163 raises AttributeError (ats_score is a column on Optimization, not Compilation), so every opted-in user's weekly digest task dies before sending and the error is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` at lines 199-201 on an ignore_result task. However, the whole path is gated behind `settings.EMAIL_ENABLED` (default False) and a non-empty DATABASE_URL, so today the digest never runs at all; the breakage becomes user-visible only once email delivery is enabled. Fix is to average Optimization.ats_score joined via resume_id/user_id (or drop the metric).
evidence: email_worker.py:162-163: `select(func.count(), func.avg(Compilation.ats_score)).where(...)`. The `Compilation` model (models.py:240-263) declares only id, user_id, resume_id, device_fingerprint, job_id, status, pdf_path, compilation_time, pdf_size, error_message, created_at — no `ats_score`. An AST sweep of every ORM attribute reference in backend/app confirms this is the only nonexistent attribute in the codebase. The enclosing `try` ends at line 200 with `except Exception as exc: logger.error(f"EMAIL: weekly digest failed for user {user_id}: {exc}")`, and the task is on Celery Beat: `"weekly-digest-monday-9am": {"task": "app.workers.email_worker.send_weekly_digest_to_all", "schedule": crontab(hour=9, minute=0, day_of_week="monday")}`.
repro: With EMAIL_ENABLED=1 and a user having email_notifications.weekly_digest=true, run `celery -A app.core.celery_app call app.workers.email_worker.send_weekly_digest --args='["<user_id>"]'` → worker logs "weekly digest failed ... type object 'Compilation' has no attribute 'ats_score'", no email sent.

title: GET /subscription/current returns 404 for any user with more than one subscription row (guaranteed after a retried or upgraded checkout)
impact: After a user abandons one Razorpay checkout and clicks Select Plan again (or activates the free plan then upgrades), the billing page permanently shows the red error box "Subscription not found" with a Retry button instead of their subscription — including for paying customers, who then cannot see status/renewal date or press Cancel.
fix: Add `.limit(1)` and use `.scalars().first()` (and ideally filter to non-cancelled rows), so the newest subscription is returned deterministically.
corr: Confirmed with narrowed impact: get_user_subscription (backend/app/services/payment_service.py:940-944) uses scalar_one_or_none() on an unlimited query, so any user with 2+ subscriptions rows (normal after a retried checkout or free-then-upgrade, since both _create_free_subscription and _create_paid_subscription unconditionally db.add a row and subscriptions.user_id has no unique constraint) raises MultipleResultsFound, which the broad except swallows into None and routes.py:951-955 returns as 404. The billing page (frontend/src/components/billing/SubscriptionManager.tsx:30-33,59-67) then permanently shows the error box with Retry instead of the subscription card, so users cannot see status/renewal date or use the in-page Cancel button. Paid feature gating is NOT affected (it reads User.subscription_plan/subscription_status), and the /subscription/cancel endpoint itself still works (it also reads from User) — it is only unreachable through this UI. Fix: add .limit(1).
evidence: `select(Subscription).where(Subscription.user_id == user_id).order_by(Subscription.created_at.desc())` has no `.limit(1)` and is consumed with `subscription_result.scalar_one_or_none()`. With >1 row SQLAlchemy raises `MultipleResultsFound` (verified locally: `MultipleResultsFound: Multiple rows were found when one or none was required`), which is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` → `return None`, and the route then does `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Subscription not found")`. Multiple rows are normal: `_create_free_subscription` does `db.add(Subscription(...))` and every `_create_paid_subscription` call does another `db.add(Subscription(...))`.
repro: POST /api/v1/subscription/create twice for the same user (e.g. planId=free then planId=pro), then GET /api/v1/subscription/current → 404. Or load /billing after two checkout attempts.

title: Nothing prevents creating a second live Razorpay subscription — plan switch double-bills the customer
impact: A Pro subscriber who clicks Basic (or re-clicks Pro after an abandoned checkout) ends up with two active Razorpay subscriptions and is charged twice every cycle; the app has lost the pointer to the first one, so `cancel_subscription` (which uses `user.subscription_id`) can never cancel it. It also permanently breaks /subscription/current (see the MultipleResultsFound finding).
fix: Before creating a new subscription, look up any existing subscription in `created/authenticated/active/pending` state; either reject with a "cancel or use upgrade flow first" error or cancel/replace the old Razorpay subscription atomically, and disable/label the current plan's card in the UI.
corr: Core defect confirmed: `create_subscription`/`_create_paid_subscription` never check for an existing subscription and never cancel the prior Razorpay subscription, and the frontend offers "Select Plan" on every plan regardless of the user's current plan. Corrected impact/severity (medium-high rather than unqualified high): the newly created Razorpay subscription starts in "created"/unpaid state, so an abandoned second checkout does not itself cause a charge — its concrete effect is that `User.subscription_id` is overwritten, orphaning the still-active original subscription so `cancel_subscription` can never cancel it (silent continued billing with no in-app way to stop it). True double-billing occurs only when the user actually authorizes the second payment link (e.g. a Pro subscriber "switching" to Basic), which is a realistic flow since nothing in the UI discourages it. The claim that this "permanently breaks /subscription/current" is overstated: the MultipleResultsFound is swallowed by the broad `except` and returns None (empty state), and multiple `Subscription` rows per user already occur today via cancel-then-resubscribe.
evidence: `create_subscription()` validates the plan, coupon and billing availability but never inspects the caller's existing `User.subscription_id` / `subscription_status`; `_create_paid_subscription()` unconditionally does `self.client.customer.create(...)`, `self.client.subscription.create(...)`, inserts a new `Subscription` row and overwrites `User.subscription_id` with the new id. The old Razorpay subscription is never cancelled. On the frontend `handleSelectPlan` has no current-plan check either — `PricingCard` always renders "Select Plan" for every plan.
repro: With billing configured: subscribe to `pro`, pay, then POST /api/v1/subscription/create with `planId: "basic"` — a second Razorpay subscription + payment link is created and `users.subscription_id` is repointed.

title: cancel_subscription reports success even when the Razorpay cancel API call fails — user is told they cancelled but keeps being charged
impact: On any Razorpay API error (network blip, 5xx, stale/invalid subscription id) the customer sees "cancelled" but the Razorpay subscription is still live and keeps charging their card every cycle. Worse, the next `subscription.charged` webhook flips `User.subscription_status` back to `active`, so support sees contradictory state and nobody notices the failed cancellation.
fix: Return `{"success": False, "error": ...}` (HTTP 502) when the Razorpay cancel call raises and do not mutate local state, or record a `cancel_pending` state plus a retry job so local state never claims a cancellation that Razorpay did not accept.
corr: Confirmed with two refinements. (1) Severity is medium-high rather than unqualified high: the bug only manifests when the Razorpay cancel call actually fails (network blip, 5xx, stale/invalid subscription id), so it is a conditional billing-correctness bug, not an always-on one. Everything else in the finding is accurate: is_available() is a config-only check, the exception is swallowed, local Subscription/User rows are unconditionally marked cancelled, and the route returns success: true. (2) Additional related nuance the finding did not mention: because the call uses `cancel_at_cycle_end: 1`, local state is optimistic even on success — Razorpay keeps the subscription active until the cycle ends while the local rows read "cancelled" immediately. The fix should both propagate the Razorpay failure (return success: false / do not commit the local cancellation) and represent the pending-until-cycle-end state distinctly, plus make _handle_subscription_charged refuse to silently flip a locally-cancelled subscription back to active without flagging it.
repro: static-only: mock/force `client.subscription.cancel` to raise, call POST /api/v1/subscription/cancel → HTTP 200 `{success: true}` while Razorpay still holds an active subscription.

title: Coupon codes are validated and consumed but the discount is never sent to Razorpay — customer is shown "20% off" and charged full price
impact: Users apply a promo code, see "Coupon applied (20% off)", are billed 100% of the plan price, and their one-time redemption is burnt. Marketing campaigns are effectively a chargeback/refund generator, and coupon usage stats are wrong.
fix: Create a Razorpay Offer (or a discounted plan) for each coupon and pass `offer_id` when creating the subscription; if discounts aren't implemented, stop accepting/consuming coupons and remove the coupon UI rather than promising a discount.
corr: The defect is real as described, but severity is better characterized as high-impact/latent rather than actively firing: no application code, migration, or admin endpoint ever creates a `CouponCode` row, so the bug only manifests once an operator manually inserts a promo code into the DB. When that happens, the described outcome follows exactly — the UI shows "Coupon applied (N% off)", the Razorpay subscription is created from the full-price plan with the coupon only in `notes`, and `used_count`/`CouponRedemption` are written at subscription-creation time (before payment), so the user's single redemption is consumed even on abandoned checkouts. Fix requires creating a Razorpay Offer and passing `offer_id` on subscription create (or a discounted plan), plus moving redemption accounting to the payment-success webhook.
evidence: `_create_paid_subscription` creates the subscription from the full-price plan id and puts the coupon only in free-text notes: `"notes": {"user_id": user_id, "plan_id": concrete_plan_id, **({"coupon_code": coupon_code} if coupon_code else {})}`. There is no `offer_id`, no amount override — `grep -n 'offer|discount' payment_service.py` matches only `coupon.discount_percent` inside `validate_coupon`. Meanwhile `create_subscription` still increments `CouponCode.used_count` and inserts a `CouponRedemption` row, and the UI toasts `result.data.message` plus `(${couponState.discountPercent}% off)`.
repro: Seed a coupon row, POST /api/v1/billing/validate-coupon (valid, 20%), then POST /api/v1/subscription/create with `couponCode` — the returned Razorpay `short_url` charges the undiscounted plan amount while `coupon_codes.used_count` increments.

title: `alembic revision --autogenerate` generates a migration that DROPS the Better Auth session/account/verification tables
loc: backend/alembic/env.py:37 (`target_metadata = Base.metadata`, no include_object filter); backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial_complete_schema.py:22-60; backend/app/database/models.py (no Session/Account/Verification models)
impact: The next developer who adds a model and runs the standard autogenerate workflow gets a migration whose upgrade() destroys every login session, every OAuth account link (including the hashed passwords stored in `account.password`) and every pending verification token. Since migrations auto-run on backend startup (`alembic upgrade head`), merging such a file logs out and locks out every user and irrecoverably deletes credentials.
fix: Add an `include_object`/`include_name` hook in backend/alembic/env.py that returns False for table names in {'session','account','verification'} (Better Auth owns them), or declare read-only SQLAlchemy models for them so autogenerate sees them.
corr:
Core defect confirmed and empirically reproduced, but severity should be low/medium (latent footgun / missing guardrail), not high.

Corrected claim: `backend/alembic/env.py` sets `target_metadata = Base.metadata` with no `include_object`/`include_name` filter, while `session`, `account` and `verification` are created by `alembic/versions/0001_initial_complete_schema.py:22-60` and are deliberately NOT declared as SQLAlchemy models (see `frontend/src/lib/auth.ts:7` — they are Better Auth's tables). Running `alembic revision --autogenerate` against a DB at head therefore emits `op.drop_table('verification')`, `op.drop_table('session')`, `op.drop_table('account')` (I ran it; verified verbatim in the generated file, then deleted it).

However the claimed impact does not follow as stated. Autogenerate is not this project's workflow: none of the 40 files in alembic/versions contains the `### commands auto generated by Alembic` marker — all are hand-written — and metadata drift is so large (~200 lines of unrelated churn: NOT NULL flips on users/subscriptions timestamps, dropping uq_users_email, idx_* -> ix_* index renames, ARRAY(TEXT)->ARRAY(String) retypes) that autogenerate output is plainly unusable and cannot be committed unedited. The three drop_tables appear at line 24 directly under the "please adjust!" banner. Reaching the claimed outcome (mass logout + deletion of hashed passwords in account.password via the `alembic upgrade head` in docker-compose.yml:130 / Makefile:158) requires a developer to merge an obviously-broken migration without reading it.

Recommended fix is still worth doing and is trivial: add an include_object/include_name callback in env.py excluding {session, account, verification} (or an exclude_tables list in alembic.ini).
evidence: 0001 creates `session`, `account` and `verification` via `op.create_table(...)`, but none of the three exists in `Base.metadata`. env.py passes `target_metadata = Base.metadata` with no object/name filter. Running autogenerate against a database at head produced, verbatim: `op.drop_table('session')`, `op.drop_table('verification')`, `op.drop_table('account')`.
repro: `cd backend && DATABASE_URL=<fresh-db> .venv/bin/alembic upgrade head && .venv/bin/alembic revision --autogenerate -m x` → the generated file contains the three drop_table calls. (Static-only in production; the danger is the generated artifact.)

title: Compile Queue Priority (Feature 34) is inverted — Pro/BYOK users get the LOWEST Redis broker priority
impact: Under load, paying Pro/BYOK users' compilations and optimizations wait behind free-tier jobs — the exact opposite of the monetized behaviour the editor advertises with its "Priority Queue" badge.
fix: Swap the constants to match Redis semantics: `TASK_PRIORITY_HIGH = 0`, `TASK_PRIORITY_NORMAL = 5`, `TASK_PRIORITY_LOW = 9` (fix QUEUE_CONFIGS defaults accordingly), and add a test asserting `get_task_priority("pro") < get_task_priority("free")`.
corr: The priority mapping is genuinely inverted for the Redis broker: kombu's redis transport consumes priority sub-queues in ASCENDING order via a single BRPOP over [queue, queue:1, ... queue:9], so free-tier tasks (priority 1) are served before pro/byok/team tasks (priority 9). Fix by inverting get_task_priority() (free -> 9/highest number = lowest served, pro/byok/team -> 0) or by reversing the comment/constant semantics consistently, and also fix the hardcoded priority=1 on the intentionally-low background ATS tasks (ats_worker.py:720,806) plus the email/cleanup entries in QUEUE_CONFIGS. Severity should be MEDIUM, not high: there is no correctness, data-loss, or security impact, and the symptom only appears when a single queue carries a standing backlog containing both tiers; Pro jobs still complete, just after free ones. The upstream cause is the checklist spec itself (P1_checklist.md:2907-2912), which prescribes the inverted mapping and the incorrect claim that higher numbers mean higher priority.
evidence: `celery_app.py:122-126` configures `broker_transport_options={"priority_steps": list(range(10)),  # 0 (highest) … 9 (lowest)`, `"queue_order_strategy": "priority"}` — the file's own comment states 0 is highest. Immediately below, `celery_app.py:140-142` defines `TASK_PRIORITY_HIGH = 9`, `TASK_PRIORITY_NORMAL = 5`, `TASK_PRIORITY_LOW = 1`, and `get_task_priority()` (line 174) maps `"free": TASK_PRIORITY_LOW` (=1) and `"pro"/"byok"/"team": TASK_PRIORITY_HIGH` (=9). With `queue_order_strategy: priority` and ascending `priority_steps`, kombu drains the lowest-numbered priority sub-queue first, so free-tier tasks (1) are consumed before pro tasks (9). The checklist is itself self-contradictory at P1_checklist.md:2912 ("Celery priority range: 0 (highest) to 9 (lowest) — higher number = higher priority in most brokers"), and every submit path propagates the inverted value (`latex_worker.py:596`, `orchestrator.py:696`, `llm_worker.py:294`, `ats_worker.py:335,383`, `format_routes.py:443`).
repro: static-only. Also observable: enqueue many free-plan latex jobs then one pro job against a backlogged Redis broker; the pro job drains last.

title: Compile Settings modal offers `--shell-escape`, which the backend rejects with 422 — and docs/FINAL_REPORT.md claims this flag was removed everywhere
impact: Any user who ticks the prominently-listed `--shell-escape` option in Compile Settings and clicks Save gets a hard 422 and loses every other change made in that modal, with no indication which option is invalid. The audit doc asserts the flag is gone from the product while it is still surfaced in the UI.

But the frontend allowlist still leads with it: `api-client.ts:27` `export const ALLOWED_LATEXMK_FLAGS = ['--shell-escape', '--synctex=1', ...]`, and `CompileSettingsModal.tsx:254` marks only `--interaction=nonstopmode`, `--halt-on-error`, `--synctex=1` as `isHardcoded` (disabled), so `--shell-escape` renders as a live clickable checkbox. `handleSave` (lines 124-134) then sends `latexmk_flags: [...flags]` to `apiClient.updateResumeSettings`, which the validator rejects.

title: No error boundary anywhere in the app — any render throw is a blank white page

There are concrete throw sites: `useNotifications()` throws `new Error('useNotifications must be used within a NotificationProvider')`, and `localStorage` access in `useState` initializers (PDFPreview.tsx:100, edit/page.tsx:875) throws `SecurityError` when site data is blocked.

title: wsClient.setToken ignores the CONNECTING state, so the job WebSocket can open anonymously and every subscribe is silently rejected
impact: When the Better Auth session resolves while the WebSocket is still CONNECTING, the socket stays anonymous for its whole lifetime. Every `subscribe` for a logged-in user's own job is refused with `forbidden`, the frontend drops that error on the floor, and the editor sits on the `PDFPreview` "Compiling…" spinner forever even though the job completed. There is no timeout and no fallback (see the polling finding).
fix: In `setToken`, also handle `CONNECTING` (close and reopen, or set a flag checked in `onopen`); and have `useJobStream` subscribe to `wsClient.on('error', ...)` and surface `forbidden`/`rate_limited` as a visible failure state instead of hanging.
corr: Real but intermittent, severity medium (not high). `WSClient.setToken` only reopens on `readyState === OPEN`, so a token that resolves while the socket is still CONNECTING is stored without being applied to the in-flight handshake; because `<AuthSync />` is nested inside `<WebSocketProvider>` the first connect is always anonymous, so whenever the better-auth session resolves during the WS handshake window the socket stays anonymous and every `subscribe` for an owner-scoped job is answered with `forbidden` (ws_routes.py:105-107). `useJobStream` never listens for the `'error'` emission, so that frame is dropped and the UI stalls. Mitigating facts the finding omits: the window is bounded by the handshake duration and the socket does pick up the token on any subsequent reconnect, so the failure is transient/rare rather than permanent. Fix: also handle CONNECTING/CLOSING in `setToken` (close and reopen once the handshake settles), and surface `'error'`/`forbidden` in `useJobStream`.
evidence: `setToken`: `if (this._ws && this._ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) { close(); reopen() }` — the `CONNECTING` state is unhandled, so a token that arrives mid-handshake is stored but never applied to the already-in-flight socket. `AuthSync` calls `wsClient.setToken(session?.session?.token ?? null)` and on first render `useSession()` has not resolved, so `WebSocketProvider`'s `wsClient.connect()` opens with no `?token=`. Backend: `if not await _job_ws_access_ok(job_id, ws_user_id): await _send_error(websocket, "forbidden", ...)`, and `_job_ws_access_ok` returns `job_owner is None or job_owner == user_id`. `useJobStream` only registers `wsClient.on('event', ...)` — it never listens for `'error'`, so the `forbidden` frame is discarded.
repro: static-only. Deterministic trigger: make `/api/auth/get-session` resolve faster than the WS handshake (typical on a warm local backend + remote WS), then start a compile as a logged-in user.

title: The documented REST polling fallback for job status is unreachable by construction, and the main editor has no fallback at all
impact: If the WebSocket never delivers events (proxy stripping WS upgrades, anonymous-socket `forbidden`, or the job finishing before the subscribe frame lands — first subscribe sends no `last_event_id`, and `event_bus.subscribe` only replays when one is supplied), the compile spinner never resolves. The user's PDF is sitting on the server but the UI shows "Compiling…" indefinitely with no error and no retry.
fix: Poll whenever `jobId` is set and the stream state is not terminal (include `'idle'`), and add a `getJobState` fallback poll to the editor page so a completed job always resolves the spinner.
corr: The documented REST polling fallback in frontend/src/hooks/useJobStatus.ts is effectively dead code: its interval effect (and refresh()'s post-fetch guard) require state.status to be 'queued'/'processing', but that state is produced only by WebSocket events, so in the WS-unavailable case status stays 'idle' and polling never starts. Additionally, refresh() only invokes callback refs and never dispatches into the jobStream reducer, so REST snapshots could not update the hook's returned status/progress/isComplete even if polling ran. The main editor (frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:991-993) uses useJobStream directly with no REST fallback at all. Corrected impact: this is a resilience gap, not a UI hang. Because isCompiling derives from the same WS-only status, a fully dead WebSocket leaves the editor showing "LaTeX editor ready" with an enabled Compile button — the failure is silent (PDF preview never refreshes after the "Compilation started" toast), and Download still works because handleDownload falls back to compileJobId. Transient disconnects are already covered by ws-client's persistent subscriptions, exponential-backoff reconnect, and last_event_id stream replay; the unrecoverable cases are WS blocked/unauthorized for the job's whole lifetime, or a job completing before the first subscribe frame (no replay without last_event_id). Severity: medium.
evidence: `useJobStatus`'s header comment claims "REST polling fallback via apiClient.getJobState() when WS is unavailable". The polling effect is gated by `if (!jobId || (state.status !== 'queued' && state.status !== 'processing')) return`, and `refresh()` re-checks the same condition at line 115. But `state` comes from `useJobStream`, which dispatches `__reset__` → `initialState.status === 'idle'` and only leaves `'idle'` when a WebSocket event arrives.
