So when the WS is down/unauthorized — the only case the fallback exists for — status is permanently `'idle'` and the interval is never created. Separately, the editor uses `useJobStream(compileJobId)` / `useJobStream(aiJobId)` directly (lines 983-985) and contains zero `getJobState` calls, so it has no fallback whatsoever.
repro: static-only. Reproduce by blocking `/ws/jobs` at the proxy and starting a compile: the spinner never terminates.

title: Offline drafts are write-only: saved drafts are never loaded back, and reloading while offline kicks the user out of the editor
impact: A user who edits offline, then reloads or navigates back to the resume before reconnecting, gets "Failed to load resume" and is bounced to /workspace (which then also renders "No resumes found") — their locally-saved draft exists in IndexedDB but nothing in the UI can reach it. Signing out silently destroys unsynced work. The reconnect flush also blind-overwrites server content with the local draft with no conflict detection despite the type modelling one.
fix: On load failure (or when `!navigator.onLine`), hydrate the editor from `getDraft(resumeId)` and show a "restored local draft" banner; warn before `clearAllDrafts()` if `pendingDraftCount() > 0`; use the `conflict` status by comparing `updated_at` before the flush PATCH.
corr: The core defect is real: offline drafts are write-only (no `getDraft` caller anywhere), sign-out unconditionally deletes still-'pending' drafts, and the reconnect flush blind-overwrites the server with no conflict detection despite the type modelling 'conflict'. Two corrections: (1) the precise offline-reload symptom depends on entry path — a hard reload while offline is served next-pwa's `/offline.html` document fallback, while a client-side navigation back to the resume produces the "Failed to load resume" toast and the `/workspace` bounce; either way the IndexedDB draft is unreachable. (2) Contributing root cause the finding omits: the service worker's API cache rule `urlPattern: /\/resumes($|\?)/` (frontend/next.config.js:45) matches neither `/resumes/{id}` nor `/resumes/?page=...`, so the intended NetworkFirst offline fallback is dead code. Severity is better characterised as medium-high, since the loss window requires the user to have explicitly pressed Save while offline.
evidence: `getDraft(resumeId)` and `markSynced` are exported but `rg "getDraft|markSynced"` finds no caller anywhere in `src`. The editor's load path is unconditional: `const data = await apiClient.getResume(resumeId)` … `catch { toast.error('Failed to load resume'); router.push('/workspace') }` — there is no offline branch that falls back to `getDraft`. Meanwhile `OfflineBanner` tells the user "edits are saved locally and will sync when you reconnect", and `handleSignOut` runs `await Promise.all([clearAllDrafts(), clearCompileQueue()])`, deleting drafts whose `syncStatus` is still `'pending'`. The `'conflict'` status in the `OfflineDraft` type is never produced or consumed.
repro: Open a resume, go offline, edit, click Save ("Saved locally"), reload the page. Result: error toast + redirect, draft unreachable.

title: Workspace dashboard swallows all load errors in production and renders the empty state instead
impact: When the backend is down, returns 500, or the session token is rejected with 401, an existing user with 20 resumes is shown "No resumes found — Create your first resume". They reasonably conclude their data was deleted. There is no retry affordance and no indication anything failed.
fix: Track a `loadError` state, render a distinct error panel with a Retry button, and special-case 401 by redirecting to /login rather than rendering the empty state.
corr: Real but medium, not high. `frontend/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:163-167` swallows initial-load failures (dev-only console.error, no toast/error state), and because the three calls are in a `Promise.all` a failure of `listResumes` or `listJobs` leaves `resumes` at `[]`, so the render at lines 761-777 shows "No resumes found — Create your first resume" with no error indication or retry. No error boundary exists (`no error.tsx`/`global-error.tsx` under frontend/src/app) and there is no 401 interceptor, so a down/500 backend or a backend-rejected session produces a misleading empty state. Impact is a misleading UI and missing retry affordance, self-correcting on reload — no data loss and no persistent corruption, so medium severity. Fix: add an error state and render a failure panel with a retry button, matching the `toast.error` convention used by every other handler in the same file.
repro: Stop the backend (or let the session expire) and load /workspace.

title: Auth token is silently dropped if the session resolves while the WebSocket is still CONNECTING, leaving real-time permanently dead for logged-in users
impact: A logged-in user whose Better Auth session resolves during the WS handshake window gets an anonymous socket. Every subscribe to their own job is rejected with `forbidden`, so no progress, no log lines, no llm.token streaming, and no job.completed ever arrives. Because there is no idle timeout on /ws/jobs and the client never re-handshakes, real-time stays dead until a full page reload.
fix: In `setToken`, treat any non-null `_ws` whose state is OPEN *or* CONNECTING as stale: close it and reopen with the new token (or, better, send the token as a first `{type:"auth"}` frame after open so no reconnect is needed).
corr: Real but medium severity, not high. WSClient.setToken only re-handshakes when the socket is already OPEN, so a token that resolves while the socket is CONNECTING is stored in _token but never applied to the in-flight socket, which then remains anonymous. That socket's subscribes to owner-scoped jobs are answered with `forbidden` (ws_routes.py:_job_ws_access_ok), and there is no working fallback (useJobStatus only polls after a WS event has moved status off `idle`, and the main workspace pages use useJobStream with no polling), so the user sees a job that appears to hang. Scope corrections: (a) the race window is only the initial page-load handshake overlapping the Better Auth get-session fetch, not a deterministic failure; (b) it is not permanent until reload — any socket close triggers _scheduleReconnect -> _openSocket, which re-reads the now-set _token and self-heals. Fix should also cover the mirror case the finding missed: a sign-out during CONNECTING leaves the socket holding the previous authenticated identity. Suggested fix: in setToken, handle CONNECTING (and any non-null _ws) by closing and reopening, or set an onopen guard that re-handshakes if _token changed since the socket was created.
evidence: setToken only re-handshakes when the socket is already OPEN: `if (this._ws && this._ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) { this._ws.close(...); ... this._openSocket() }`. There is no branch for `CONNECTING` — the token is stored in `_token` but the in-flight socket was built in `_openSocket()` with `if (this._token) url.searchParams.set('token', this._token)` evaluated *before* the token existed, so that socket stays anonymous for its entire lifetime. On the server, `_job_ws_access_ok` then returns False for any job whose meta has a `user_id` (`return job_owner is None or job_owner == user_id`) and the subscribe is answered with `_send_error(websocket, "forbidden", ...)`.
repro: Load /workspace/<id>/edit while signed in with the WS endpoint slower than the session fetch (or throttle the WS handshake); subscribe returns {type:"error",code:"forbidden"} and the editor never receives compile events. Static-only otherwise.

title: WebSocket onclose handler does not check socket identity, so a token change leaks an orphaned live socket and can double-deliver every event
impact: Every login/logout (token change) leaks one permanently open WebSocket per browser tab on the server. If any job subscription is active at that moment, `onopen` on both sockets replays `_subscriptions`, so every event is delivered twice into a reducer that is not idempotent — `case 'llm.token': streamingLatex: state.streamingLatex + event.token` doubles every token, corrupting the LaTeX written into Monaco, and `log.line` duplicates every compiler log line. The `connected` flag also flips false while a socket is actually open.
fix: Capture the socket in a local (`const ws = new WebSocket(...)`) and guard every handler with `if (this._ws !== ws) return` before mutating state or scheduling reconnects; explicitly null handlers on the socket you intentionally discard.
corr: The defect is real: `ws.onclose` in frontend/src/lib/ws-client.ts:167-175 never compares the closing socket to `this._ws`, so `setToken` (and `disconnect()`+`connect()`) orphans the newly created socket — the old socket's onclose nulls the reference to it and schedules a third connection, leaving the second socket permanently open with `onmessage` attached (the backend has no idle timeout or per-user cap to reap it). Corrected impact/severity (medium, not high): the guaranteed consequence is one leaked client+server WebSocket per token change per tab. Duplicate event delivery is a narrower race — it only occurs if a job is already in `_subscriptions` when the token changes, since the orphan can never receive later `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` frames; when it does occur, that job's events double for the tab's lifetime and corrupt the non-idempotent reducer (`streamingLatex + event.token`, `log.line` appends). The `connected` flag flip is transient and cosmetic.
evidence: `setToken` does `this._ws.close(); this._ws = null; this._openSocket()` — `_openSocket` assigns `this._ws = ws2` synchronously, but the *old* socket's handler fires later and unconditionally does `this._ws = null; this._emit('disconnected', ...); if (!this._manuallyDisconnected) this._scheduleReconnect()`. It never compares the closing socket against `this._ws`, so it nulls the reference to ws2 and schedules a third socket. ws2 is never closed and still has `onmessage = ... this._handleMessage(...)` attached.
repro: Sign in (or let a session refresh change the token) while a compile/optimize job is streaming: the editor content becomes duplicated token soup and the server logs two 'WebSocket connection accepted' entries that never both close. Static-only reachable by reading the handler.

title: Server-sent WebSocket error frames have zero listeners, so 'forbidden'/'rate_limited'/'invalid_request' are silently swallowed
impact: Every server-side rejection is a no-op in the UI: the user sees a job 'submitted' toast and then nothing forever, with no error, no retry, and no diagnostic. This is the failure mode that makes the two auth bugs above invisible instead of loud.
fix: Register an `error` handler in WebSocketProvider that surfaces the code via NotificationProvider/toast, and have useJobStream dispatch a synthetic failure state when a `forbidden` error arrives for the job it is watching.
corr: Server-sent WebSocket `{"type":"error"}` frames have no listeners: `_emit('error', ...)` in ws-client.ts:216-221 iterates an empty handler set (same for 'subscribed'), and the frame is not even console-logged. In practice the only reachable code is 'forbidden' from `_job_ws_access_ok` (ws_routes.py:107, 130) — 'invalid_request'/'unknown_message_type' cannot be produced by this client and 'rate_limited' needs >20 msgs/sec that the client never generates. Consumers routed through useJobStatus recover anyway via its 5s `GET /jobs/{id}/state` poll (useJobStatus.ts:140-147), but consumers that use useJobStream directly (edit, optimize, cover-letter, try pages, QuickTailorModal, CompareModal, InterviewPrepPanel, useFormatConversion) have no fallback and will spin indefinitely with no error surfaced. Severity: medium — a diagnostic/robustness gap that makes the WS auth-token race silent, not an independent high-severity failure.
evidence: `_handleMessage` emits `this._emit('error', {code, message})`, but a repo-wide search for `wsClient.on(` finds only `on('connected')`/`on('disconnected')` in WebSocketProvider.tsx:58-59 and `on('event')` in useJobStream.ts:46. Nothing subscribes to `'error'` or `'subscribed'`. Meanwhile the server answers subscribe/cancel failures with `{"type":"error","code":"forbidden"|"rate_limited"|"invalid_request"}`.
repro: Subscribe to a job owned by another user (or reuse an anonymous socket for an owned job): the backend sends the error frame, the browser drops it, the UI spins indefinitely.

title: First subscribe never requests replay, so all events published before the subscribe frame lands are lost with no recovery path
impact: `job.queued` is structurally impossible for the client to observe, and for a fast job (short compile) `job.completed` itself can be published before the subscribe frame arrives. The reducer then stays at `status: 'idle'`, so `isProcessing = stream.status === 'queued' || 'processing'` is false on /try and the PDF fetch effect never fires — the user clicks Compile, gets a success toast, and nothing happens at all, permanently. None of the primary pages (try, optimize, edit, cover-letter, QuickTailorModal) have any REST reconciliation.
fix: Have useJobStream subscribe with `last_event_id: '0'` (or the earliest known id) so the server replays the whole stream from the beginning, making the reducer's accumulate-from-scratch model correct on first attach and on remount.
corr: Real but overstated. Accurate part: the first WS subscribe never requests replay, so every event published before the subscribe frame lands is dropped — `job.queued` is always lost, and the pages using useJobStream directly (/try, optimize, edit, cover-letter, QuickTailorModal) have no REST reconciliation (useJobStatus' polling fallback is gated on queued/processing so it cannot rescue an 'idle' stream). Overstated part: losing job.queued is cosmetic because the reducer promotes to 'processing' on job.started/job.progress; the "stuck at idle forever, nothing happens" outcome requires the terminal event inside a few-millisecond window while events only originate from a separate Celery worker after the HTTP response (no eager mode, no compile-result cache), so it is realistic only for an immediate worker-pickup failure or a remount/reload after events were emitted. Severity: medium latent correctness gap, fix is one line (pass '0' as last_event_id on first subscribe, optionally plus a one-shot apiClient.getJobState reconcile).
evidence: `useJobStream` calls `wsClient.subscribe(jobId)` with no second argument, and `event_bus.subscribe` only replays when a value is passed: `replayed = 0; if (last_event_id): replayed = await self._replay_events(...)`. Yet `job.queued` is XADDed *and* published inside `_write_initial_redis_state` before the HTTP submit response is even returned, and workers start publishing `job.started`/`job.progress`/`log.line` the instant the Celery task picks up — all before React renders the new jobId and the subscribe frame reaches the server.
repro: Submit a trivial compile that finishes in <100ms (warm worker) and watch the reducer stay idle; or add latency to the WS subscribe frame. Backed by the code paths above.

title: Pages that fetch on mount send unauthenticated requests (auth token race with AuthSync)
impact: On direct navigation / refresh / new tab: /settings shows "Failed to load preferences" and reports GitHub/Zotero/Mendeley/Dropbox as all disconnected (those `.catch(() => {})` swallow the 401); /admin shows "Failed to load" with a raw `HTTP 401` string (its 403 sniffing `msg.includes('403')` misses 401); /admin/tenant toasts "Failed to load tenants"; /workspace/builder/[resumeId] toasts an error and force-redirects to /workspace, so a builder draft cannot be opened by URL at all. Works only when soft-navigating from an already-loaded page.
fix: Gate these effects on the resolved session (`const {data: session, isPending} = useSession(); if (isPending || !session) return`) like /workspace does, or make `request()` fall back to `credentials: 'include'` plus a same-site cookie so the first paint's requests authenticate.
corr: Core defect confirmed but severity should be medium-high, and it is one root cause rather than four independent bugs. The only genuinely high-impact instance is frontend/src/app/workspace/builder/[resumeId]/page.tsx:285-306, where the 401 triggers toast + router.push('/workspace'), making a builder draft unopenable by direct URL or refresh with no recovery. frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx:69-92 degrades visibly (error banner plus integrations falsely shown disconnected) but is recoverable on any subsequent interaction/soft navigation. frontend/src/app/admin/page.tsx:23-34 and frontend/src/app/admin/tenant/page.tsx:64-79 are admin-only surfaces with essentially cosmetic failure. All four stem from one missing auth-readiness gate: fix once in AuthSync/api-client (expose an auth-ready promise the request() awaits, or add credentials:'include' plus backend CORS allow_credentials) or via a shared useAuthedEffect, rather than patching four pages.
evidence: `request()` never sets `credentials`, so the `better-auth.session_token` cookie is not sent cross-origin (frontend :5180 → API :8030, and `api.<domain>` in production per frontend/.env.production.example). The only auth is `headers()`: `const token = this.authToken ?? (typeof window !== 'undefined' ? localStorage.getItem('auth_token') : null)`. Nothing in the repo ever writes `localStorage.setItem('auth_token', ...)` (grep: only two reads, lines 887 and 1781). `authToken` is set by `AuthSync`'s `useEffect` from `session?.session?.token`, and better-auth's `useAuthQuery` starts with `{data: null, isPending: true}` (node_modules/better-auth/dist/client/query.mjs:6-11) and fetches asynchronously. Pages listed above call `apiClient.*` in a mount effect with no `session` guard, so on a hard load the request goes out with no Authorization header.
repro: Sign in, then hard-reload http://localhost:5180/workspace/builder/<resumeId> (or /settings, /admin). Observe 401 in the network tab and the error path.

title: Signed-out visitors get a permanent loading spinner instead of a login redirect on five pages
impact: A signed-out user (or one whose session expired) who opens a shared/bookmarked editor URL sees an eternal spinner on a black screen. On /workspace/[id]/edit and /optimize it is worse: `GlobalHeader` returns `null` for those paths (`fullscreenPatterns` in components/GlobalHeader.tsx:30,45-47), so there is no nav, no sign-in link, and no way out except editing the URL.
fix: Add the guard used elsewhere: `useEffect(() => { if (!sessionLoading && !session) router.push('/login') }, ...)` and set the page's loading flag to false when there is no session; or add real auth gating in middleware.ts for /workspace*, /workspaces*, /dashboard, /settings, /billing, /developer, /tracker, /admin.
corr: Core defect confirmed, severity should be medium rather than high. Signed-out (or expired-session) visitors to /workspace/[id]/edit, /workspace/[id]/optimize, /workspaces, /workspaces/[id], and /workspaces/[id]/recruiter get a permanent LoadingSpinner because the fetch effect early-returns on a missing session while isLoading/loading stay true, and none of the five pages does the router.push('/login') that seven sibling pages do. On /edit and /optimize the page is chrome-less (GlobalHeader.tsx:30 fullscreenPatterns returns null and MarketingFooter.tsx:8-9 hides itself), so there is no in-page nav or sign-in link — though browser back/reload still works. On the three /workspaces* routes GlobalHeader renders normally, so the user has a visible sign-in path and the defect is only a spinner where an empty state or redirect belongs. No data loss or security exposure; the dead `if (!session?.user) return null` branches should be replaced with an actual redirect.
evidence: Editor page: `const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true)` and the loader effect starts with `if (sessionLoading || !sessionData) return` — `setIsLoading(false)` only runs in the `finally` of `fetchResume`, which never executes. Render then hits `if (isLoading) return <LoadingSpinner />`. Same shape in optimize (`if (!session || sessionLoading) return`). /workspaces: `if (!session?.user) return` in the effect, then `if (sessionLoading || loading) return <LoadingSpinner />` — `loading` stays `true` forever, making the following `if (!session?.user) return null` dead code. None of these five pages contain a `router.push('/login')`, unlike /workspace, /dashboard, /tracker, /byok, /workspace/merge, /workspace/cover-letters.
repro: Sign out (or open a private window) and visit /workspace/<any-uuid>/edit, /workspace/<uuid>/optimize, /workspaces, /workspaces/<uuid>, or /workspaces/<uuid>/recruiter.

title: Workspace resume list is hard-capped at 20 with no pagination — extra resumes and their variants become unreachable
impact: A user with more than 20 resumes silently cannot see or open the rest from the main workspace — no indicator that anything is missing. Worse, a variant whose `parent_resume_id` is on page 2 is filtered out of `masterResumes` and its `variantMap` bucket is never rendered, so it disappears entirely.
fix: Use `listResumesPaginated` and add page controls (or an infinite-scroll/load-more), and show `total` so truncation is visible.
corr: Confirmed as a real but medium-severity defect: `apiClient.listResumes()` defaults to `limit=20` and drops the backend's `total`/`pages` metadata, and /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/frontend/src/app/workspace/page.tsx has no pagination UI, so a user with more than 20 non-archived resume rows (masters and variants share those 20 slots, ordered by `updated_at desc`) silently sees only the 20 most recently updated, with no "showing 20 of N" indicator. Client-side search/tag filtering also cannot reach off-page rows. Variants whose parent row falls outside the page are not rendered at top level, and expanding a master only shows variants that happen to be in the same 20 rows — visibly inconsistent with the server-computed `variant_count` badge. The same unpaginated call pattern also affects /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/frontend/src/app/workspace/merge/page.tsx:47, /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/frontend/src/app/workspaces/[workspaceId]/page.tsx:46, and /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/frontend/src/components/AddApplicationModal.tsx:48. Not data loss (resumes remain reachable via direct /workspace/{id}/edit URLs), so this is a discoverability/UX defect rather than high severity. Fix: use the existing `listResumesPaginated`, or raise the limit (backend clamps at 100) plus a load-more/count indicator, and fetch variants via the backend's already-supported `parent_id` filter on expand.
evidence: The page calls `apiClient.listResumes()` with no arguments; the client signature is `listResumes(page = 1, limit = 20, archived = false)` hitting `/resumes/?page=1&limit=20`, and the backend paginates (`offset = (page - 1) * limit`) returning `{resumes, total, page, limit, pages}` — but `listResumes` throws away everything except `data.resumes`. The page has no page state, no "load more", and never reads `total`/`pages` (grep for `page`/`pagination` in workspace/page.tsx finds only `listResumes(1, 50, true)` for the archived modal). Rendering is `masterResumes.map(...)` where masters/variants are derived from that single 20-row page.
repro: Create 25 resumes, open /workspace: only 20 cards render and there is no pagination control.

title: No MinIO/S3 configuration in any production manifest — storage_service silently targets http://localhost:9000
loc: backend/app/core/config.py:110-114, backend/app/services/storage_service.py:28-36, docker-compose.prod.yml (no minio service, no MINIO_* env), k8s/backend/deployment.yaml (no MINIO_* env)
impact: In production every storage operation (template PDF/thumbnail upload and retrieval, presigned download URLs) fails with a connection error to localhost:9000 with empty credentials — the template gallery and any S3-backed export are broken, and the failure mode is a runtime 500 rather than a startup error.
fix: Add a MinIO (or managed S3/R2) service plus MINIO_ENDPOINT/ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY/BUCKET to docker-compose.prod.yml and to the k8s secret + backend deployment env; the .env.production template should list them too.
corr:
Core config gap is real but the description and severity are overstated; corrected claim (medium, deployment-manifest hygiene rather than a code defect):

Verified true:
- /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/core/config.py:110-114 does default MINIO_ENDPOINT="http://localhost:9000", MINIO_ACCESS_KEY="", MINIO_SECRET_KEY="", MINIO_BUCKET="latexy".
- /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/services/storage_service.py:_get_client() builds the boto3 client from exactly those settings (module-level singleton).
- /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/docker-compose.prod.yml has no minio service and no MINIO_* env (and no env_file); /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/k8s/backend/deployment.yaml has no MINIO_* env and no envFrom/secretRef. Only docker-compose.yml and backend/docker-compose.yml set them.

Corrections to the finding:
1. Not "silent": config.py:549-559 (CONFIG-001) already logs a startup WARNING when MINIO_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY are in {"minioadmin","minioadmin_secret",""} and is_production_like() — empty creds are explicitly covered.
2. Failure mode is not a 500. template_routes.py:220-289 wraps every storage call in try/except, logs, and returns HTTP 502 "Storage unavailable" (or 404). Share/anon-PDF paths (resume_routes.py:1734-1741, routes.py:1160-1178) catch exceptions and degrade gracefully with logger.warning. Presigned-URL generation makes no network call at all, so it returns a syntactically valid but unreachable http://localhost:9000/... URL instead of erroring.
3. "Template gallery broken" is wrong. Listing, detail, and latex_content come from Postgres (ResumeTemplate); only PNG/PDF previews are storage-backed, and frontend/src/components/TemplateCard.tsx:48-58 already renders a placeholder on image failure. Template selection and compilation still work.
4. docker-compose.prod.yml is not a usable deployment path anyway: its backend env omits BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and JWT_SECRET_KEY, which are hard-required in Settings.model_post_init (raises ValueError at import). So that file would fail to boot before any storage call — MinIO is one of several missing vars in an incomplete manifest, not a distinct storage bug. The genuine, reachable gap is the k8s manifest set: k8s/backend/deployment.yaml supplies the startup-fatal secrets but no MINIO_* and there is no MinIO/S3 object-storage resource under k8s/, so in a k8s deploy thumbnail/PDF preview endpoints return 502 and presigned share URLs point at localhost:9000.

Recommended fix: add MINIO_ENDPOINT/ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY/BUCKET (from latexy-secrets) to k8s/backend/deployment.yaml + celery deployment, provision an S3/MinIO backend, and either fix or delete docker-compose.prod.yml; optionally promote the CONFIG-001 warning to a hard startup failure when endpoint is localhost in production-like envs.
evidence: config.py defaults `MINIO_ENDPOINT="http://localhost:9000"`, `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=""`, `MINIO_SECRET_KEY=""`. storage_service.py builds the boto3 client from exactly those settings. docker-compose.prod.yml defines nginx/frontend/backend/celery/redis/postgres/prometheus/alertmanager/tempo/exporters/grafana — no MinIO — and passes no MINIO_* vars; the k8s backend deployment env list has no MINIO_* keys either (only the dev docker-compose.yml sets them).
repro: static-only: grep for MINIO_ in docker-compose.prod.yml and k8s/ returns nothing.

title: FRONTEND_URL and BETTER_AUTH_URL are never set in production, so share links, e-mails and OAuth redirects point at http://localhost:5180
impact: Users who create a share link, request student verification, or complete a Zotero/Mendeley/Dropbox OAuth flow in production get a localhost:5180 URL — the share feature produces unusable links and the OAuth callbacks redirect the browser off-site to nothing.
fix: Set FRONTEND_URL (and BETTER_AUTH_URL) to the public origin in docker-compose.prod.yml, .env.production and k8s/backend/deployment.yaml.
corr: FRONTEND_URL (only) defaults to http://localhost:5180 in backend/app/core/config.py:142 and is not set in any production deployment artifact (.env.production, backend/.env.example, docker-compose.prod.yml, k8s/), and nothing validates it at startup. Under docker-compose.prod.yml it cannot even be supplied via the host shell because the backend service uses an explicit `environment:` list with no `env_file`. Consequently, unless the operator manually adds the variable, backend-generated absolute URLs point at localhost: share links (resume_routes.py:101, 1779 — the frontend copies share_url verbatim in ShareResumeModal.tsx:213), student-verify links (payment_service.py:178), team invites (team_routes.py:146), digest/notification emails (email_service.py, email_worker.py:87), and the github/zotero/dropbox/mendeley OAuth callback redirects. The BETTER_AUTH_URL part of the finding is incorrect: it is set in .env.production:72, in k8s via the latexy-config `frontend-url` key (k8s/backend/deployment.yaml:92) and in frontend/.env.production.example:22 — and the backend never reads settings.BETTER_AUTH_URL to build any URL. Severity: medium — a documented/templated env var omission, fixable by adding FRONTEND_URL to the env examples, compose and k8s env blocks (reusing the existing frontend-url configMap key) and failing startup in model_post_init when is_production_like() and FRONTEND_URL still points at localhost.
evidence: config.py: `FRONTEND_URL: str = Field(default="http://localhost:5180")`. resume_routes.py:101 `self.share_url = f"{settings.FRONTEND_URL}/r/{self.share_token}"`; payment_service.py:178 `verify_url = f"{settings.FRONTEND_URL}/billing?student_verify={token}"`; mendeley/dropbox callbacks `RedirectResponse(f"{settings.FRONTEND_URL}/settings?...")`. docker-compose.prod.yml's backend env block contains neither FRONTEND_URL nor BETTER_AUTH_URL (k8s at least maps BETTER_AUTH_URL from the configMap frontend-url, but still no FRONTEND_URL).
repro: static-only: POST a share-link creation on a prod-configured backend; response share_url is http://localhost:5180/r/<token>.

title: TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is never enabled behind nginx, so all anonymous traffic shares one rate-limit bucket
impact: In production every unauthenticated request is attributed to the nginx container/pod IP, so RATE_LIMIT_CALLS_PER_MINUTE=60 / PER_HOUR=1000 becomes a global cap shared by all anonymous visitors — one crawler starves everyone — and per-IP abuse controls stop distinguishing clients.
fix: Set TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true in the production backend env (compose + k8s), since the app is always fronted by the bundled nginx there.
corr: Real but medium, not high. In any nginx-fronted deployment (docker-compose.prod.yml, k8s/nginx), TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is never set, so backend/app/middleware/rate_limiting.py:_spoof_resistant_client_id falls back to the nginx peer IP and all *anonymous* requests share one 60/min / 1000/hr bucket, causing spurious global 429s for unauthenticated visitors. Authenticated users are keyed by session-token hash and unaffected; nginx still enforces genuine per-IP limits (api 10r/s burst 20, login 5r/m, limit_conn 10) and anonymous compile/trial quotas are keyed on device fingerprint, so this is an availability/false-429 defect, not a loss of all per-IP abuse control or a quota-theft vector. The fix must not simply flip the flag: nginx sets X-Forwarded-For via $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (client-appended) while the code reads split(',')[0], so it should parse the right-most untrusted hop (or use X-Real-IP) before trusting proxy headers.
evidence: rate_limiting.py `_spoof_resistant_client_id`: `client_ip = request.client.host ...; if getattr(settings, "TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS", False): forwarded_for = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For") ...`. config.py defaults it to False, and `rg TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS` finds no producer in docker-compose.prod.yml, k8s/, or .env.production — while both nginx configs do set X-Forwarded-For.
repro: static-only: no manifest sets TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true, and the default branch ignores X-Forwarded-For.

title: XeLaTeX / LuaLaTeX are offered in the UI but not installed in the backend/worker images; failure is retried for ~7 minutes while the UI shows "processing"
impact: A user who picks XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX (the documented way to get custom fonts/Unicode) gets a compile that appears stuck at "Compiling…" for ~7 minutes, then fails with `error_code: "internal"` and message `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'xelatex'`. Three worker slots are burned per attempt.
fix: Add `texlive-xetex texlive-luatex` to both Dockerfiles (matching modal_app.py), and treat `FileNotFoundError` on the compiler binary as non-retryable with a clear "compiler not available" message instead of 3 exponential retries.
corr: XeLaTeX (only — not LuaLaTeX) is offered in the UI and accepted by the API but is not installed in backend/Dockerfile or backend/Dockerfile.prod: I built the exact package list and got `xelatex: MISSING`, while `lualatex: /usr/bin/lualatex` is pulled in transitively by texlive-latex-extra and compiles successfully. The break is limited to the container-image deployments (docker-compose `worker`, Dockerfile.prod) because those images have no `docker` CLI, so latex_worker.py:290-300 execs the bare binary → FileNotFoundError; the Modal image installs texlive-xetex, and the hybrid dev setup has the docker CLI and falls back to texlive/texlive:latest. The failure is then masked: the generic `except Exception` at latex_worker.py:544 retries 3x (60+120+240 = 420s of delay), publishing only `job.retrying`, which useJobStream.reducer.ts does not handle, so the UI stays at "Compiling…" for ~7 minutes before a terminal `error_code: "internal"`. The "three worker slots burned per attempt" claim is wrong — countdown retries are re-scheduled via ETA and do not occupy a concurrency slot. Fixes: add `texlive-xetex` to both Dockerfiles, and treat FileNotFoundError / missing-binary as non-retryable with a clear error message (or preflight `shutil.which(compiler)` before enqueueing/compiling and gate the UI options on it).
evidence: `ALLOWED_LATEX_COMPILERS: List[str] = ["pdflatex", "xelatex", "lualatex"]` and `CompileSettingsModal` renders all three (`{ id: 'xelatex', label: 'XeLaTeX', desc: 'Unicode + custom fonts' }`). Both Dockerfiles install only `texlive-latex-base/-extra/-recommended/-fonts-*` — `grep xetex\|luatex` matches only `backend/modal_app.py:60-61 ("texlive-xetex", "texlive-luatex")`. docker-compose.yml:158-161 builds `worker` from the same `backend/Dockerfile`, and that container has no `docker` CLI, so `shutil.which("docker")` is falsy and the worker execs the bare `compiler` binary → `FileNotFoundError`. That lands in the task's generic `except Exception`, where `retryable = self.request.retries < self.max_retries` → `self.retry(countdown=min(60 * (2 ** retries), 600))` three times, publishing only `job.retrying` — an event the reducer ignores (no `case 'job.retrying'` in useJobStream.reducer.ts).
repro: PATCH /resumes/{id}/settings {"compiler":"xelatex"} then click Compile in the Docker deployment.

title: LaTeX compile errors are never shown to the user; the status bar says "LaTeX editor ready" after a failed compile
impact: When a compile fails on a LaTeX error, the user sees the preview go blank, no toast, and a red status line reading "LaTeX editor ready". The actual reason ("! Undefined control sequence") exists only if the user manually switches to the Logs tab. The captured `first_latex_error` is thrown away.
fix: Add a `compileStream.status === 'failed'` branch to `statusText` that renders `compileStream.error`, fire a `toast.error` in the failure effect, and include `first_latex_error` in the worker's `job.failed` `error_message` so the message has the actual TeX error and `l.N` context.
corr: Real but overstated. The genuine defect is narrow: `statusText` in frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:1779-1789 has no `compileStream.status === 'failed'` branch, so after a failed compile the footer renders "LaTeX editor ready" in rose instead of the failure message, and `compileStream.error` is never displayed anywhere (only the `compile_timeout` banner at 2904 exists). Separately, backend `latex_worker.py` captures `first_latex_error` and includes it only in the task result as `latex_error_line`, which no frontend code consumes, and the `job.failed` event carries only a generic "<compiler> exited with code N". BUT the error reason is not hidden from the user: every pdflatex line, including the "! ..." line, is streamed as a `log.line` event with `is_error=true`, rendered rose by LogViewer, and `runCompile` switches the right pane to the Logs tab (page.tsx:1392) before the job starts, with the pane header showing status "failed". The only path with no failure signal is the intentionally silent auto-compile. Severity: medium/low (confusing status text + unused structured error), not high.
evidence: `statusText` has branches for `isAiRunning`, `isCompiling`, `compileStream.status === 'completed'`, `aiStream.status === 'completed'`, `aiStream.status === 'failed'` — and then `: 'LaTeX editor ready'`. There is no `compileStream.status === 'failed'` branch, even though the footer colors itself rose for exactly that case (`aiStream.status === 'failed' || compileStream.status === 'failed' ? 'text-rose-400/80'`). `grep 'compileStream.error'` in the page returns nothing — the value is never rendered. The only failure-specific UI is the `errorCode === 'compile_timeout'` banner at line 2904. The effect at 1097-1104 handles `compileStream.status === 'failed'` by calling `apiClient.trackCompilation(...,'failed')` with no toast. On the backend, the worker captures `first_latex_error` (`if first_latex_error is None and stripped.startswith("!")`) and puts it in the task *result* as `latex_error_line`, but the `job.failed` event it publishes carries only `"error_message": f"{compiler} exited with code {proc.returncode}"`.
repro: In the editor, type `\badcommand` before `\end{document}` and click Compile.

title: BYOK API keys are never used by the main optimize / quick-tailor flows — the platform key always pays
impact: A paying BYOK-plan user who has added and validated their OpenAI key still runs every resume optimization, combined job and Quick Tailor on the platform's key — the platform absorbs 100% of the token cost the BYOK plan was designed to offload, and the user gets neither their own rate limits nor their own model access.
fix: In job_routes.submit_job and resume_routes.quick_tailor_resume, resolve `await api_key_service.get_user_provider(db, user_id, "openai")` and pass it as `user_api_key=` to both submit helpers (as cover_letter_routes already does).
corr: Core claim confirmed; scope/severity should be tightened. (a) It is a billing/cost-correctness and feature-promise defect, not a security issue — better rated medium-high than high. (b) BYOK is not "never used": cover letter generation, document/format conversion, ATS scoring (ats_routes.py:737) and the inline AI endpoints (ai_routes.py `_resolve_ai_api_key`, which correctly prefers the user's key and even rate-limits the platform-key fallback) all resolve the user key. The gap is specific to the three job types that go through job_routes `submit_job` (`llm_optimization`, `combined`) and `resume_routes.quick_tailor_resume`. (c) Note for the fix: `submit_*` forward kwargs into the Celery broker / Modal spawn payload, so naively passing the decrypted key would put plaintext provider secrets in Redis task payloads — the fix should resolve the key inside the worker (or pass a reference), not just add the kwarg. `ai_routes._resolve_ai_api_key` is the pattern to mirror.
evidence: orchestrator/llm_worker both do `api_key = user_api_key or settings.OPENAI_API_KEY`, but no caller of the two main job types passes `user_api_key`: job_routes' `submit_resume_optimization(...)` (llm_optimization) and `submit_optimize_and_compile(...)` (combined) omit the kwarg entirely, and so does `quick_tailor_resume`. Only cover_letter_routes.py:298-321 and format_routes.py:421-440 resolve a key (`api_key_service.get_user_provider(db, user_id, "openai")`). Meanwhile billing sells a BYOK plan (frontend/src/app/billing/page.tsx:55 MONTHLY_PLAN_IDS includes 'byok') and job_routes.py:255-258 comments "Client-chosen model is only honoured for paid/BYOK plans, else the default model runs on the platform key".
repro: Add an OpenAI key via /byok/api-keys, then POST /jobs/submit {job_type:"combined"} and inspect the worker: `user_api_key` is None so `settings.OPENAI_API_KEY` is used. static-verifiable by grep: `user_api_key` appears in no job_routes/resume_routes submit call.

title: Client-supplied `model` string is forwarded to the platform OpenAI key with no allowlist
loc: backend/app/api/job_routes.py:97 (`model: Optional[str] = None`), :258 (safe_model), :383/:409; consumed at orchestrator.py:377 and llm_worker.py:90
impact: Any pro/byok/team subscriber can pick the most expensive model in the OpenAI catalogue (e.g. an o-series/reasoning model priced hundreds of times higher per token than the default gpt-4o-mini) for every optimization, billed to the platform account. Also lets a client select a model that does not exist or does not support the parameters sent, turning a normal optimize into a hard `job.failed`.
fix: Validate `request.model` against an explicit server-side allowlist (e.g. the keys of a MODEL_PRICING/permitted-models map) and reject anything else with 422; only honour arbitrary models when the request is actually executed on the user's own key.
corr: Client-supplied `model` is forwarded unvalidated (no allowlist) to the OpenAI call that runs on the platform key (`settings.OPENAI_API_KEY`), gated only by plan family at job_routes.py:258. Real but medium severity, not high: requires an authenticated pro/byok/team subscription, output tokens are capped at OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS=4000 and requests are rate-limited (60/min, 1000/hr), so it is a cost-abuse/hardening gap (a paid user can select a far more expensive model billed to the platform) rather than an unauthenticated billing drain. The secondary "invalid or incompatible model -> job.failed" effect is self-inflicted only and not a DoS. Fix: validate `model` against a per-plan allowlist in the same place `compiler`/`persona` are validated.
evidence: `safe_model = request.model if resolve_plan_family(resolved_plan) in {"pro", "byok", "team"} else None` — the only check is the plan family; the string itself is never validated against an allowlist. It is passed straight into `client.chat.completions.create(model=model or settings.OPENAI_MODEL, ...)`. Because of the previous finding, that call is authenticated with `settings.OPENAI_API_KEY`, not the user's key.
repro: POST /jobs/submit {job_type:"combined", model:"o1-pro"} as a pro-plan user → orchestrator calls OpenAI with model="o1-pro" on the platform key.

title: Cancelling a job during LLM streaming is turned into a retry (second full LLM call) and reported as a hard failure
impact: Pressing Cancel (or closing QuickTailorModal, which calls cancel()) does not cancel: the task is retried, a second full LLM completion is billed, and the user finally sees "Tailoring failed / internal" instead of "cancelled". QuickTailorModal treats 'failed' and 'cancelled' identically and shows a red "Tailoring failed" panel for a user-initiated cancel.
fix: Use a dedicated sentinel (e.g. `class JobCancelled(Exception)`), catch it before the generic handler, publish `job.cancelled` and return without retrying — the same treatment llm_worker/cover_letter_worker already give in-stream cancellation.
corr: Cancelling during LLM streaming raises a generic RuntimeError that the orchestrator's catch-all treats as retryable, so the task is retried once (60s later), starts a second LLM stream that aborts again ~20 tokens in, then emits a terminal job.failed/error_code="internal". Real but low severity: cancellation itself works, only a partial second completion is billed, and the UI is unaffected because both cancel paths publish job.cancelled immediately, useJobStream.reducer.ts ignores later terminal events (job.retrying isn't handled at all), and QuickTailorModal closes/unsubscribes on cancel. The only user-observable leak is the REST snapshot latexy:job:{job_id}:state being overwritten to "failed", plus wasted worker/LLM spend. Fix with a dedicated cancellation exception (or an is_cancelled() check in the except handler / before starting the LLM stream on retry).
evidence: Inside `_run_llm_stage`: `if token_count % 20 == 0 and is_cancelled(job_id): raise RuntimeError("Job cancelled during LLM streaming")`. The caller has no special case for it: `except Exception as exc: ... if self.request.retries < self.max_retries: publish_event(job_id, "job.retrying", ...); raise self.retry(...)`, else `publish_event(job_id, "job.failed", {"error_code": "internal", ...})`. The cancel flag is `latexy:job:{job_id}:cancel` with a 3600s TTL (ws_routes.py:376), so it is still set on the retry, which starts a brand-new streaming completion and dies again ~20 tokens in.
repro: Start a combined/quick-tailor job, click Cancel while tokens are streaming → observe job.retrying then job.failed(error_code=internal, message "Job cancelled during LLM streaming") and two OpenAI calls.

title: No output-truncation guard: 4000-token cap on a whole-document rewrite, finish_reason never checked, silent fallback to the unmodified resume
impact: For any resume longer than roughly 4k output tokens (long/2-page or academic CVs) the model is cut off mid-document. llm_worker then publishes `llm.complete` + `job.completed` with success=true while `optimized_latex` is byte-identical to the input — the user is told the optimization succeeded and sees zero changes, with nothing in the logs. In the orchestrator the truncated document is instead compiled, so the run dies with a confusing LaTeX error.
fix: Compute the prompt token count and size `max_tokens` from the model's context window (or reject/split inputs that cannot round-trip); capture `chunk.choices[0].finish_reason` and, when it is "length", fail the job with an explicit `error_code: "output_truncated"` instead of silently returning the original.
corr: Real defect, but scope it: the 4000-token completion cap only bites when the optimized document (plus the CHANGES JSON) exceeds ~4k tokens, i.e. long/2-page/academic CVs, not all resumes — so medium-to-high rather than unqualified high. Also, in llm_worker the user does see the truncated document stream in via llm.token events before llm.complete overwrites full_content with the original, so the observable symptom is "content appeared then reverted to the original with success=true and no log line", not literally "zero changes with no signal". The orchestrator does have a JSON-parse fallback with a warning at orchestrator.py:474-496, but it only fires when the parsed LaTeX is empty, so it does not cover truncation. Fix is to (a) size max_tokens from the discarded count_tokens(prompt) result or drop the cap, and (b) inspect finish_reason == "length" (available on the last stream chunk) and fail the job loudly instead of silently returning fallback_latex.
evidence: The prompt asks for "[Complete optimized LaTeX document here]" plus a JSON change list, but the completion cap is `max_tokens=settings.OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` = 4000 with no comparison against the input size (`llm_service.count_tokens(prompt)` is called at llm_service.py:213 and its result thrown away). `grep -rn finish_reason app/` returns hits only in llm_provider_service — none of the streaming workers ever inspect `finish_reason == "length"`. In llm_worker the truncated case degrades silently: `parse_delimited_optimization` needs both markers, so a response with `<<<LATEX>>>` but no `<<<END_LATEX>>>` returns `fallback_latex` (the original resume) — and the warning is suppressed because its guard is `if optimized_latex == latex_content and "<<<LATEX>>>" not in accumulated`, which is False here.
repro: Submit a ~15k-character LaTeX resume as job_type="llm_optimization" with OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS=4000 → job.completed with optimized_latex == input and no warning.

title: LLM-generated LaTeX is compiled by the orchestrator without the shell-escape/file-write validation the direct compile path enforces
impact: A job posting containing prompt-injection text ("add \\input{/etc/passwd} to the preamble", "emit \\write18{...}") can get those primitives into the compiled document. When `shutil.which("docker")` is false the compiler runs locally in the worker with the app's filesystem, so `\input`/`\lstinputlisting` of a server file lands in the PDF the user downloads; the optimized LaTeX is also echoed back into the editor and persisted as a checkpoint.
fix: Call `latex_service.validate_latex_content(optimized_latex)` (and strip/reject `\input`/`\include`/`\openin` with absolute or ../ paths) before writing and compiling LLM output, and neutralise the delimiter markers plus obvious instruction text in `job_description`/`custom_instructions` before interpolating them into the prompt.
corr: The orchestrator's combined pipeline (backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:522-568) compiles LaTeX without the validate_latex_content guard that the compile-only worker and the /compile routes apply — and its callers (job_routes.py:399,634; resume_routes.py:1132,1250) do not validate the user-supplied input latex_content either. So the whole optimize+compile path is unvalidated on both input and output; the simplest exploit is a user embedding file-read primitives in their own resume (prompt injection via job_description/custom_instructions is a secondary, less reliable route). Because no --shell-escape is passed and texmf is unmodified, \write18 gives restricted shell-escape rather than RCE; the realistic impact is exfiltration of server files/secrets (e.g. /proc/self/environ, .env) into the PDF the requester downloads via \input/\verbatiminput/\lstinputlisting, since the compiler runs as a local binary in the worker container (no docker CLI in backend/Dockerfile*, no docker.sock mount). Severity: medium, not high.
evidence: latex_worker guards every user-submitted document: `if not latex_service.validate_latex_content(latex_content):` which rejects `_SHELL_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?:write18|openout|openin|input18)\b")`. `_run_latex_stage` in the orchestrator receives the *model's* output and goes straight to `tex_file.write_text(latex_content, encoding="utf-8")` followed by Popen(compiler …) with no validation call at all. The model's output is steerable by untrusted text: `_create_optimization_prompt` interpolates `job_description` verbatim (ai_routes/job_routes accept up to 10k chars, and job_scraper_service/scraper_routes fetch job descriptions from arbitrary remote pages) directly above the output-format instructions.
repro: static-only: compare latex_worker.py:209 (validate) with orchestrator.py:544 (no validate) on the same class of content.

title: The combined optimize+compile job path never calls validate_latex_content at all
impact: Even the intended (if weak) shell-escape / absolute-`\input` guard is absent on this route, so `\write18{...}` and `\input{/etc/passwd}` — the literal forms the blacklist was written to stop — go straight to pdflatex. Any hardening applied to the validator alone is bypassed by choosing job type `combined`.
fix: Move validation into a single choke point (e.g. at the top of `_run_latex_stage` and `run_latex_subprocess`, not in the callers) so every compile path — including the LLM-rewritten output — is validated before pdflatex sees it.
corr: The validation gap is real: the `combined` job path (backend/app/api/job_routes.py:387-412 -> orchestrator.optimize_and_compile_task -> _run_latex_stage at backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:522-565) and /resumes/{id}/quick-tailor (backend/app/api/resume_routes.py:1126-1146) never call latex_service.validate_latex_content, unlike the latex_compilation path (backend/app/workers/latex_worker.py:209) and the sync routes (backend/app/api/routes.py:363,548,757). No Pydantic validator, dependency, or middleware compensates. However the claimed impact is overstated and severity should be MEDIUM, not high: (1) the raw user latex_content is not compiled on this path -- _run_latex_stage receives `optimized_latex`, the LLM's regenerated output (orchestrator.py:162-166), so a payload must survive an LLM rewrite; (2) `\write18{...}` does not yield code execution because neither the Docker nor the local compile command passes --shell-escape (orchestrator.py:545-565) and pdflatex's default restricted mode rejects arbitrary shell commands; the realistic primitive is `\input{/abs/path}` file disclosure echoed into the job's streamed log.line events; (3) in the production Docker path the compile runs in a throwaway container mounting only job_dir, so disclosure is container-scoped -- host file reads require the local-binary fallback, and the attacker only reads into their own job stream (no cross-tenant exposure). Correct fix: invoke validate_latex_content inside _run_latex_stage so both combined and quick-tailor are covered.
evidence: `grep -n validate_latex_content backend/app` matches only latex_worker.py:209 and routes.py:363/548/757. job_routes.py's `combined` branch checks only `if not request.latex_content or not request.latex_content.strip()` before `submit_optimize_and_compile(latex_content=request.latex_content, ...)`, and `orchestrator._run_latex_stage` writes that content straight to `tex_file.write_text(latex_content)` and compiles it. `/resumes/{id}/quick-tailor` reaches the same orchestrator path.
repro: POST /jobs with `{"job_type":"combined","latex_content":"...\\input{/etc/passwd}...","job_description":"x"}` and observe the log.line stream.

title: Two per-route rate limiters trust X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, contradicting TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS and letting anonymous callers bypass the anti-abuse caps
impact: One unauthenticated client rotating `X-Forwarded-For` (and `device_fingerprint`) can consume the entire platform-wide 500 deep-analyses/hour budget on the operator's OpenAI key, and can drive the scraper's outbound fetches without limit — using the service as a request relay against third-party job boards.
fix: Replace both local `_client_ip` helpers with `middleware.rate_limiting._spoof_resistant_client_id` (peer IP unless TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS, credential-derived when authenticated), and add a per-session/global cap that does not depend on client-supplied identifiers.
corr:
The code defect is real but the severity and impact are overstated. Real part: ats_routes.py:59-64 and scraper_routes.py:52-63 both honour X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, while the shared middleware helper (middleware/rate_limiting.py:25-51) gates XFF on settings.TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS (default False, config.py:192). Both per-route IP buckets (ratelimit:deepanalyze:ip:{ip}, cache:ratelimit:scrape:{ip}) are therefore client-forgeable — an inconsistency worth fixing by routing both helpers through one settings-aware function.

Overstated parts: (1) /ats/deep-analyze has an XFF-independent global backstop of 500/hr checked immediately after the IP check (ats_routes.py:678-684), so an attacker can monopolize but not exceed the shared anonymous budget — it is quota-exhaustion/DoS on a bounded pool, not unbounded spend on the operator OpenAI key. (2) RateLimitMiddleware is on by default (RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=True, 60/min + 1000/hr, main.py:138-143) and keys on the unspoofable peer IP when TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is false, so a single source IP is capped at 60/min / 1000/hr across all routes; the scraper is not "without limit", it just degrades from 10/min to that global ceiling. (3) The relay/SSRF concern is separately mitigated by the scraper's private/link-local/metadata IP rejection (services/job_scraper_service.py:38-52, 883). (4) The device_fingerprint rotation bypass was already anticipated (comment at ats_routes.py:666-669) — the IP and global limiters run before the flag/fingerprint logic. Corrected severity: medium.
evidence: The shared limiter documents the rule — "X-Forwarded-For is only honoured behind a trusted proxy (TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS)" — but `ats_routes._client_ip` does `forwarded = http_request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For"); if forwarded: return forwarded.split(",")[0].strip()` and `scraper_routes._client_ip` does the same with no settings check. These feed `ratelimit:deepanalyze:ip:{ip}` (limit 10/h, guarding the LLM-backed `/ats/deep-analyze` that the code itself annotates "burns the platform OpenAI key") and `cache:ratelimit:scrape:{ip}` (10/min on the unauthenticated URL fetcher). The anonymous trial gate next to it keys on a client-supplied `device_fingerprint`, and when the `deep_analysis_trial` flag is off the comment says "unlimited deep analysis for all".
repro: curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.<n>' -X POST http://localhost:8030/scrape-job-description -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}' in a loop with incrementing n — never 429s. Same for POST /ats/deep-analyze.

title: k8s manifests ship committed Secrets with known weak passwords that deploy.sh applies as-is
impact: Anyone who has read the public repo knows the datastore credentials of a cluster deployed with the provided scripts; if Postgres/Redis is reachable from any other pod or an exposed service, the full user database, session tokens and encrypted BYOK blobs are accessible. Unlike .env.production (which contains only placeholders), these are applied values.
fix: Delete the Secret bodies from the repo; generate them at deploy time (`kubectl create secret generic ... --from-env-file`) or source them from a sealed-secret/external-secrets provider, and have deploy.sh abort if the secret does not already exist.
corr: k8s manifests commit real Secret objects with hardcoded weak passwords (postgres.yaml:17-18 latexy_password_123, redis.yaml:41-42 redis_password_123, and the same values plus flower-auth admin:flower123 inside k8s/namespace.yaml's latexy-secrets), and k8s/deploy.sh applies all three unmodified with no validation. Since the repo is public these are known default credentials, and with no NetworkPolicy in k8s/ any pod in the cluster can authenticate to postgres-service:5432 / redis-service:6379. But both datastore Services are type ClusterIP (only nginx/nginx.yaml:253 is LoadBalancer), so there is no direct internet exposure — an attacker needs pod-network or cluster access first. The manifests are labeled "change this in production" and every other secret is a YOUR_..._HERE placeholder that forces the operator to edit namespace.yaml anyway, and nothing in the docs/CI invokes k8s/deploy.sh. Severity: medium (default-credentials landmine in deployment scaffolding), not high. Fix: replace the literal data with stringData placeholders or generate the secrets in deploy.sh (openssl rand), strip the plaintext comments, and add NetworkPolicies restricting postgres/redis to backend+worker pods.
evidence: postgres.yaml: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: bGF0ZXh5X3Bhc3N3b3JkXzEyMw==  # latexy_password_123`; redis.yaml: `REDIS_PASSWORD: cmVkaXNfcGFzc3dvcmRfMTIz  # redis_password_123` — both real Secret objects (not templates), with the plaintext helpfully written in the adjacent comment. `deploy.sh` runs `kubectl apply -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/database/postgres.yaml"` and `.../redis/redis.yaml` unmodified. (Separately, docker-compose.prod.yml:324 defaults Grafana admin to `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_PASSWORD:-admin}`.)
repro: static-only: base64 -d the Secret values, then `kubectl apply -f k8s/redis/redis.yaml` uses them verbatim.

title: BYOK key-list proxy mangles the backend response shape, crashing the /byok settings page
impact: Any user who has saved a BYOK key gets a client-side TypeError rendering /byok, so they cannot see or delete their stored provider keys — the BYOK management UI is non-functional despite the backend working.
fix: In the proxy, pass the backend body through (`return NextResponse.json(data)`) or destructure correctly: `{ success: true, api_keys: data.api_keys ?? [], total_count: data.total_count ?? 0 }`, and defensively `Array.isArray(keys) ? keys : []` in the component.
corr: The defect is real but the trigger condition is understated: the crash happens for EVERY authenticated user loading /byok, including users with zero saved keys, because the backend always returns a truthy response object so `apiKeys.length` is `undefined` (never 0) and `apiKeys.map` always throws. It also breaks ProviderSelector (`userApiKeys.some(...)` at ProviderSelector.tsx:61) via the onKeysChange callback, not just APIKeyManager. The `total_count: data.length || 0` part of the evidence is inert — no consumer reads total_count. Fix: in frontend/src/app/api/byok/api-keys/route.ts return the backend payload through directly (e.g. `api_keys: Array.isArray(data.api_keys) ? data.api_keys : [], total_count: data.total_count ?? 0`).
evidence: The backend returns `UserAPIKeysResponse` = `{success, api_keys: [...], total_count}`. The Next.js proxy then does `const transformedData = { success: true, total_count: data.length || 0, api_keys: data || [] }` — `data` is the object, so `data.length` is undefined (total_count 0) and `api_keys` becomes that same object. `APIKeyManager` does `const keys = data.api_keys || []; setApiKeys(keys)` and later `apiKeys.length === 0 ? ... : apiKeys.map(...)`; with an object, `.length` is undefined (so the empty branch is skipped) and `.map` is not a function.
repro: Add an API key via POST /api/byok/api-keys, then load /byok — `apiKeys.map is not a function`.

title: Batch Tailor variants are never updated with the tailored LaTeX — every variant is a byte-identical copy of the parent
impact: The advertised outcome ("Submit up to 10 job descriptions — get a tailored resume variant for each") does not happen. Users pay for N LLM optimizations and then open N variants that contain the original, un-tailored resume. The optimized text exists only in a 24h Redis job result and in an auto-save Optimization checkpoint the batch UI never links to.
fix: Have the orchestrator (or a small follow-up task) UPDATE `resumes.latex_content = optimized_latex WHERE id = :resume_id` when the job was submitted by batch tailor (e.g. a `persist_to_resume=True` kwarg), keeping the checkpoint as the undo point.
corr: Core claim confirmed: no worker or route ever updates the forked Resume.latex_content, so a batch variant opened via the "View" link shows the parent's original LaTeX, not the tailored output. Correction to the impact framing: the tailored LaTeX is not only in a 24h Redis result — the orchestrator's record_auto_save_checkpoint writes it as an `Optimization` row keyed to the variant's own resume_id (dedup never fires since the fork is new), and that row is exposed by GET /resumes/{resume_id}/checkpoints and restorable from the variant's version-history panel in the editor. So this is a persistence/UX gap requiring an undiscoverable manual "restore checkpoint" step, not irrecoverable data loss. Severity medium-high rather than high.
evidence: create_batch_tailor forks the resume with `latex_content=parent.latex_content` and submits `submit_optimize_and_compile(..., resume_id=str(fork.id))`. The orchestrator uses that resume_id for exactly two things: `record_auto_save_checkpoint.apply_async(args=[_resume_id, user_id, optimized_latex], queue="cleanup")` and the completion email. No worker ever issues an UPDATE against `Resume.latex_content` (`grep -n "update(Resume" app/workers/*.py` → no matches; only cover_letter_worker.py:332 updates a row). The UI's success action is `<Link href={`/workspace/${job.variant_resume_id}/edit`}>View</Link>`.
repro: POST /jobs/batch with one job entry, wait for status completed, then GET /resumes/{variant_resume_id} — latex_content equals the parent's verbatim.

title: Cancelling a combined job during LLM streaming triggers a full retry (second billed LLM call) and reports "internal error" instead of cancelled
impact: Pressing Cancel costs the operator (or a BYOK user) a second complete LLM completion plus a 60s delay, and the durable Redis stream/state ends in `failed` rather than `cancelled`, so anything replaying the stream or polling /jobs/{id}/state after reload sees a bogus internal error.
fix: Raise a dedicated `JobCancelled` exception (or return a sentinel) from `_run_llm_stage`, catch it before the generic handler, publish `job.cancelled`, and return without retrying; also check `is_cancelled(job_id)` once at the top of the task.
corr:
Core defect is real but the impact description is overstated in two ways.

Verified as claimed:
- /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:410-411 — `if token_count % 20 == 0 and is_cancelled(job_id): raise RuntimeError("Job cancelled during LLM streaming")` inside `_run_llm_stage`, with no surrounding try/except that classifies it.
- The task (`optimize_and_compile_task`, decorator at orchestrator.py:63-70, `max_retries=1, default_retry_delay=60`) catches it in the generic `except Exception` at :294-313 and, on attempt 1, publishes `job.retrying` and `raise self.retry(countdown=min(60*(2**0),600))` = 60s. There is no `except`/isinstance branch for cancellation and no `revoke()` anywhere in backend/app (grep for "revoke" returns nothing).
- The cancel flag is `setex(latexy:job:{id}:cancel, 3600, "1")` in both cancel paths (app/api/job_routes.py:901 and app/api/ws_routes.py:376), so it is still set on the retry; the retry re-enters `_run_llm_stage`, re-issues `client.chat.completions.create(..., stream=True)`, and raises again. Second time `self.request.retries (1) < max_retries (1)` is false, so it publishes `job.failed` with `error_code: "internal", error_message: "Job cancelled during LLM streaming"`.
- No `is_cancelled()` check at task entry (the first checks are at :148 and :169, i.e. *after* the LLM stage), so a job cancelled while queued still opens a paid LLM stream.
- `_update_state_snapshot` (app/workers/event_publisher.py:140-157) maps job.failed → "failed", so `latexy:job:{id}:state` (read by GET /jobs/{id}/state) ends in `failed`, not `cancelled`. The cancel endpoints never write the state snapshot at all, so /state also reports "processing" between cancel and the eventual failure.

Overstated:
1. "a second complete LLM completion" — the retry aborts again after ~20 streamed deltas, so the extra billed cost is essentially the prompt tokens (full LaTeX + JD, non-trivial) plus ~20 output tokens, not a full completion.
2. "reports internal error" to the user — the frontend is already guarded. /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/frontend/src/hooks/useJobStream.reducer.ts:80-91 (CANCEL-02) ignores any terminal event once status is terminal, so the provisional `job.cancelled` published synchronously by the cancel endpoint wins, and the later `job.failed` is dropped both live and on stream replay after reload. The bogus "Job failed" only surfaces through the REST fallback in useJobStatus.ts:125-126 when the WS never delivered job.cancelled (WS degraded), and in any external consumer that reads the state snapshot/last stream event rather than the reducer.

Corrected severity: medium. Real fix is a dedicated cancellation exception (or an is_cancelled() re-check in the except handler) that publishes job.cancelled and returns without retrying, plus an is_cancelled() check at task entry.
evidence: Inside `_run_llm_stage`: `if token_count % 20 == 0 and is_cancelled(job_id): raise RuntimeError("Job cancelled during LLM streaming")`. That RuntimeError lands in the task's generic `except Exception:` which does `if self.request.retries < self.max_retries: ... raise self.retry(...)`. The cancel flag is `setex(f"latexy:job:{job_id}:cancel", 3600, "1")`, so it is still set on the retry — the retry re-runs the whole prompt build + `client.chat.completions.create(...)` and raises again, and the second time the handler publishes `job.failed` with `error_code: "internal", error_message: "Job cancelled during LLM streaming"`. There is also no `is_cancelled()` check at task entry, so a job cancelled while queued still starts a paid LLM stream.
repro: Submit a combined job, DELETE /jobs/{job_id} while tokens are streaming; worker logs show "Orchestrator task ... raised: Job cancelled during LLM streaming" followed by a retry and a second OpenAI stream.

title: Collab WebSocket accepts legacy HS256 JWTs, bypassing the LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED kill switch that the REST path enforces
impact: Any HS256 token signed with JWT_SECRET_KEY (a separate secret from BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, and one that is not rotated when legacy auth is turned off) authenticates on the collaboration socket even with LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED=false, granting read/write access to any resume that principal owns or collaborates on. The documented kill switch does not actually close this path.
fix: Replace the fallback with `if getattr(settings, "LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED", False): user_id = auth_middleware.user_id(token)`, or better, call `get_current_user_optional`'s logic directly so both transports share one code path.
corr: The collab WebSocket (/ws/collab/{resume_id}) does bypass the LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED kill switch: ws_routes.py:274 calls the legacy HS256 validator unconditionally while the REST dependency gates the identical fallback. However the impact is narrower than claimed: exploitation requires a token validly signed with JWT_SECRET_KEY (signature and exp are verified), and the owner/collaborator authorization check still applies, so this is a defense-in-depth / kill-switch-consistency defect (the documented switch does not close every legacy path, leaving a standing forgery surface if JWT_SECRET_KEY leaks) rather than a directly exploitable auth bypass. Severity low-to-medium. Fix: wrap the fallback in `if getattr(settings, "LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED", False)` or, better, factor the two-step token resolution into one shared helper used by both REST and WS paths.
evidence: ws_routes.py: `user_id = await _validate_better_auth_session(token, db)` then `if not user_id: user_id = auth_middleware.user_id(token)` — an unconditional call into `_LegacyJWTValidator`. The REST dependency deliberately gates the same fallback: "Legacy JWT fallback — OFF by default. Better Auth is the sole token issuer; this stateless path is only enabled for an explicit migration window (settings.LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED) to avoid a standing forgery surface" followed by `if getattr(settings, "LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED", False): return _jwt_validator.user_id(token)`. `/ws/jobs` correctly uses `_validate_better_auth_session` only; `/ws/collab/{resume_id}` does not.
repro: static-only: set LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED=false, mint jwt.encode({'sub': <victim_or_attacker_user_id>, 'exp': ...}, JWT_SECRET_KEY, 'HS256'), connect to /ws/collab/{resume_id}?token=<jwt>. REST calls with the same token return 401; the WebSocket accepts it.

title: Public portfolio exposes every non-archived resume of the user, with no per-resume visibility flag
impact: Flipping the single "enable portfolio" switch publishes the titles, ids and timestamps of ALL of the user's resumes — including private per-company tailored variants created by batch-tailor, whose titles embed company and role names — to anyone who knows or guesses the username. There is no way to exclude a resume short of archiving it.
fix: Add an explicit per-resume visibility column (e.g. `portfolio_visible boolean default false`) and filter the query on it, or restrict the listing to resumes that currently have a non-null `share_token`.
corr: GET /portfolio/{username} does lack a per-resume visibility filter — it returns all non-archived resumes of an opted-in user with no auth, contradicting its own "public resumes" contract, and batch-tailor fork titles do embed company names (job_routes.py:580). But the leak is metadata-only (id, title, created_at, updated_at — no LaTeX/structured content/PDF/job description), role names are not included (they live only in Redis batch metadata), the exposed resume UUIDs are not exploitable anonymously (public access requires share_token; all /resumes/{id} routes enforce get_current_user_required plus a user_id ownership predicate), and it requires explicit opt-in since portfolio_enabled defaults to false with no frontend UI that enables it. Fix is to add a per-resume public flag (or reuse share_token/tags) to the query filter. Severity: low, not medium.
evidence: `get_portfolio` docstring says "returns profile + public resumes for a username", but the query is `select(Resume).where(Resume.user_id == user.id, Resume.archived_at.is_(None))` — the only gate is the account-level `users.portfolio_enabled`. The Resume model has no public/visibility column (the only portfolio fields on User are `portfolio_enabled`, `portfolio_custom_domain`, `portfolio_theme`, `portfolio_tagline`), and there is no filter on tags, `is_template`, or share state. The route requires no auth at all.
repro: POST /portfolio/setup to enable a portfolio, create a variant via POST /jobs/batch-tailor (titles derived from company/role), then GET /portfolio/{username} unauthenticated — every variant is listed.

title: `dropbox_sync_enabled` is missing from `ResumeResponse`, so the editor's Dropbox sync state is always false after reload
impact: After any page reload, an editor with Dropbox sync enabled shows the toggle as off and hides the Push/Pull buttons (edit/page.tsx:2026). Clicking the toggle calls `enableDropboxSync` again instead of `disableDropboxSync`, so users cannot turn sync off from the editor.
fix: Add `dropbox_sync_enabled: bool = False` (plus folder_path/last_sync_at to match the GitHub fields) to `ResumeResponse` and to the `_resume_response_from_obj` payload, or have the editor initialize from `GET /dropbox/resumes/{id}/status`.
corr: Real defect, with the impact narrowed: `dropbox_sync_enabled` (and `dropbox_folder_path` / `dropbox_last_sync_at`) are absent from `ResumeResponse` and from `_resume_response_from_obj`'s payload in backend/app/api/resume_routes.py, so `GET /resumes/{id}` never serializes them. The editor at frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:1030 therefore always initializes `dbxSyncEnabled` to false after a reload, hiding the Push/Pull buttons (page.tsx:2026) even when sync is enabled server-side. The unused `apiClient.getResumeDropboxStatus` (api-client.ts:2390 → GET /dropbox/resumes/{id}/status) would have supplied it but is never called. Correction to the stated impact: disabling sync is not impossible — the first toggle click wrongly re-runs `enableDropboxSync` (extra push to Dropbox) and flips local state to true, after which a second click correctly disables. Fix by adding the dropbox fields to `ResumeResponse` + the payload dict (mirroring the github_* fields), or by calling `getResumeDropboxStatus` on load.
evidence: `grep -c dropbox backend/app/api/resume_routes.py` → 0. `ResumeResponse` explicitly lists `github_sync_enabled`, `github_repo_name`, `github_last_sync_at` but nothing for Dropbox, and `_resume_response_from_obj`'s payload dict likewise has no dropbox key. The model has `dropbox_sync_enabled: Mapped[bool]` (models.py:206). The frontend declares `dropbox_sync_enabled?: boolean` on its Resume interface (api-client.ts:275) and does `setDbxSyncEnabled(data.dropbox_sync_enabled ?? false)` from `getResume` (edit/page.tsx:1030). Since `response_model=ResumeResponse` drops unknown fields, the field is never serialized. The editor never calls the working `GET /dropbox/resumes/{id}/status` endpoint (dropbox_routes.py:57-64), so nothing masks it.
repro: Enable Dropbox sync on a resume, reload /workspace/{id}/edit — Dropbox button renders in the disabled style and Push/Pull are gone; the toggle re-enables rather than disables.

title: `GET /resumes/export/bulk` exports archived resumes despite claiming otherwise, and issues one extra query per resume in pdf mode
impact: Users who archived old/obsolete resumes get them back in the bulk export ZIP. For an account with many resumes the pdf export does N+1 DB round-trips plus N blocking S3 downloads on the event loop, stalling all other requests served by that worker for the duration.
fix: Add `Resume.archived_at.is_(None)` to the filter; fetch the latest completed Compilation for all resume ids in one grouped query, and wrap `download_bytes` in `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` / `run_in_executor`.
corr: Both issues are real but the severity is overstated. (a) `GET /resumes/export/bulk` (backend/app/api/resume_routes.py:1948-1968) omits the `Resume.archived_at.is_(None)` filter that its own docstring and `list_resumes` (lines 552-557) imply, so archived resumes are included in the ZIP. This is a correctness/UX bug over the caller's own data — `user_id` is still filtered, so there is no cross-user exposure. (b) In the `pdf` branch (lines 1999-2022) the handler issues one `Compilation` query per resume and calls the synchronous boto3 `download_bytes` (storage_service.py:55-64) without a thread offload, blocking the event loop for the duration. Real, but the impact is added latency and stalling on that worker for realistic resume counts, not a general outage. Suggested severity: low-to-medium.
evidence: Docstring: "Download all non-archived resumes as a ZIP archive." The query is `select(Resume).where(Resume.user_id == user_id).order_by(Resume.updated_at.desc())` — no `Resume.archived_at.is_(None)` filter (compare `list_resumes` at line 552-556 which does filter on `archived_at`). In the `format == "pdf"` branch the handler runs a separate `select(Compilation)...limit(1)` inside the per-resume loop, and calls the synchronous boto3 `download_bytes(compilation.pdf_path)` from an async handler with no thread offload.
repro: Archive a resume via PATCH /resumes/{id}/archive, then GET /resumes/export/bulk?format=tex — the archived resume's .tex is present in the ZIP.

title: Webhook idempotency key is read from a body field Razorpay does not send, so replay protection never actually engages and stale events can re-grant a cancelled plan
impact: The documented replay protection is dead code in production; the only real guard is the payment-id dedupe in `subscription.charged`. A Razorpay retry of an older `subscription.activated` delivered after `subscription.cancelled` silently re-grants the paid plan and pushes `current_period_end` 30/365 days into the future, so a cancelled user keeps paid features and the local state desyncs from Razorpay.
fix: Take the event id from `request.headers.get("X-Razorpay-Event-Id")` and pass it into `handle_webhook` (fall back to a hash of the raw body), and ignore state transitions whose `created_at` is older than the last processed event for that subscription.
corr: Real but lower severity (low, defense-in-depth) and mis-described impact. Accurate claim: `payment_service.handle_webhook` derives its idempotency key from a non-existent body field (`event_data.get("id")`), and the route never reads the `X-Razorpay-Event-Id` header, so the `SET … NX EX 86400` replay guard is unconditionally skipped in production and its test coverage in `backend/test/test_webhook_security.py` is vacuous (the helper synthesises `data["id"]`).
