Practical impact is limited because the handlers are effectively idempotent (`subscription.charged` dedupes on `razorpay_payment_id`; the status handlers are plain state writes), and the claimed "stale activated re-grants a cancelled plan" scenario does not follow: (a) event-id idempotency does not provide ordering guarantees anyway — that would need a `created_at`/status monotonicity check, which is genuinely absent; and (b) `_handle_subscription_activated` is reached with `entity = event_payload.get("subscription", {})` un-unwrapped at payment_service.py:528, so with a real Razorpay body `entity.get("id")` is None and the handler bails before mutating `User`. Fixes: read the event id from the `X-Razorpay-Event-Id` header (fall back to a hash of the raw body), fix the missing `_unwrap_entity` at line 528, add a monotonicity/ordering check, and make the tests use a real Razorpay envelope shape.
evidence: `event_id = event_data.get("id")` — the Razorpay webhook body is `{"entity":"event","account_id":…,"event":…,"contains":[…],"payload":{…},"created_at":…}`; the event identifier is delivered in the `X-Razorpay-Event-Id` header, which the route never reads (it only reads `X-Razorpay-Signature`). The test suite only passes because `_make_payload(..., event_id)` synthesises `data["id"] = event_id`. With `event_id` falsy the whole `SET … NX EX` guard is skipped (`if event_id:`) and every delivery is processed. There is also no ordering check on `created_at`, and `_handle_subscription_activated` unconditionally sets `User.subscription_plan = plan_id, subscription_status="active"` and extends `current_period_end` by a full period.
repro: static-only: POST the same real-shaped Razorpay body (no top-level `id`) twice with a valid signature — both are fully processed; log line "Duplicate webhook event skipped" never appears.

title: Anonymous trial use is consumed before the request is validated, so a 400 error burns one of three free uses and triggers a 5-minute cooldown
impact: An anonymous visitor whose upload is rejected (missing \begin{document}, bad encoding, unsupported compiler, or an enqueue/500) loses a third of the free trial and is additionally locked out for 5 minutes by the cooldown — the classic "I never got a single result but my trial is used up" complaint. Three malformed pastes exhaust the trial and permanently set `blocked = True`.
fix: Validate input (and successfully enqueue) before consuming the trial, or keep the check-only path and increment after a successful compile/enqueue — e.g. split into `check_trial()` under the row lock plus a `consume_trial()` on success, releasing on 4xx/enqueue failure.
corr: The increment-before-validate ordering is real in both handlers and the committed usage is never rolled back, but the reachable impact is narrower than claimed. The invalid-LaTeX/missing-content scenarios apply only to the legacy `/public/compile` route, which the frontend never calls; the live path `/jobs/submit` does no LaTeX validation at all, so malformed LaTeX legitimately consumes a worker compile. The `device_fingerprint` 400 is already checked before the increment, and the unsupported-compiler 400 is unreachable from the typed client. The genuinely reachable loss is an infrastructure failure (Redis state write or Celery enqueue raising -> 500 at job_routes.py:465-470) or a hand-crafted 400/422, after which `usage_count` has been committed and `last_used` set, costing one of three free uses plus a 5-minute cooldown. Fix is to move validation/enqueue before `check_and_track_usage` (or add a compensating decrement on failure). Severity: low, not medium.
evidence: In `/public/compile`, `trial_service.check_and_track_usage(...)` (which does `trial.usage_count += 1; trial.last_used = now` and sets `trial.blocked = True` at the limit) runs *first*; only afterwards does the handler check `if file … elif latex_content … else: raise HTTPException(400, "Either latex_content or file must be provided")` and `if not latex_service.validate_latex_content(...): raise HTTPException(400, ...)`. `submit_job` behaves the same way: the trial increment at line 271 precedes the `raise HTTPException(400, f"Unsupported compiler …")` check and the Celery enqueue, and nothing decrements on failure.
repro: POST /api/v1/public/compile with `device_fingerprint=fp_x` and `latex_content=hello` (no documentclass) → 400; then GET /api/v1/public/trial-status?fingerprint=fp_x → `usageCount: 1`, and the next valid attempt returns 429 `cooldown`.

title: Team seat members keep team/pro-level access forever after the owner's team subscription is cancelled or halted
impact: An owner buys the ₹2499 Team plan, invites 5 teammates, then cancels (or the card fails and Razorpay halts the subscription). The owner drops to free, but all 5 members retain paid-tier LLM model choice, Pro compile timeouts and 1000 API calls/day indefinitely — a permanent, free upgrade for 5 accounts per one month of payment.

title: Downgrade path 0034→0029 is impossible: 0032's downgrade drops two indexes owned by 0030
impact: Any operator rolling back below revision 0030 gets `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedObject: index "idx_account_user_id" does not exist` and the rollback aborts. Worse, downgrading only as far as 0030 succeeds but silently removes `idx_session_user_id` and `idx_account_user_id` — the two indexes backing the per-request Better Auth session lookup — even though revision 0030 is the revision that owns them. The schema no longer matches the stamped revision and auth lookups degrade to sequential scans.
fix: Remove the `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_account_user_id` / `idx_session_user_id` lines from 0032's downgrade (0032 did not create them, 0030 did), and change 0030's downgrade to `op.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ...")` for defensiveness.
corr: Real but low severity, and the performance impact is misattributed. Correct claim: 0032's downgrade drops idx_session_user_id and idx_account_user_id, which are owned by 0030, so (a) a manual `alembic downgrade` to any revision at or below 0030 aborts when 0030's downgrade calls op.drop_index on the already-removed indexes, and (b) stopping at 0030 leaves the schema out of sync with the stamped revision (both userId indexes missing). These indexes back user->session/account joins and cascade deletes, NOT the per-request session lookup, which uses session.token (idx_session_token, correctly owned by 0032). No automated path runs downgrade (all tooling only runs `alembic upgrade head`), so exposure is limited to manual operator rollback. Fix is one line each: remove the two DROP INDEX statements from 0032's downgrade, or add IF EXISTS guards in 0030's downgrade.
evidence: 0030 creates the indexes: `op.create_index("idx_session_user_id", "session", ["userId"])` and `op.create_index("idx_account_user_id", "account", ["userId"])`. 0032 re-creates them idempotently in upgrade (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_session_user_id ...`) but its downgrade unconditionally removes them: `op.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_account_user_id")` and `"DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_session_user_id"`. 0030's downgrade then calls `op.drop_index("idx_account_user_id", "account")` with no IF EXISTS.
repro: Verified on a scratch DB: `alembic upgrade head`, then `alembic downgrade 0030` (succeeds; `SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename IN ('session','account')` now returns only session_pkey, uq_session_token, account_pkey), then `alembic downgrade 0029` → ProgrammingError UndefinedObject on `DROP INDEX idx_account_user_id`.

title: pgvector extension and HNSW index on resumes.content_embedding are never used by any query
impact: Every resume save pays HNSW index-maintenance cost (plus full 1536-float array round-trips into Python) for an index the planner can never use. Semantic matching is a Python O(n) loop capped at 20 resumes, so a user's 21st+ resume is silently never ranked. README claims embeddings are 'stored as ARRAY(Float) in PostgreSQL with a [hnsw] index. Computed on save, used for /ats/semantic-match', implying DB-side vector search that does not exist.
fix: Either migrate the column to `vector(1536)` (pgvector Vector type) and push ranking into SQL with `ORDER BY content_embedding <=> :jd_emb LIMIT n` so the HNSW index is used, or drop idx_resumes_embedding_hnsw and the vector extension dependency and correct the README.
corr: Downgrade to low / documentation-and-dead-code: migration 0002 contains a `CREATE EXTENSION vector` + HNSW expression-index attempt that is intentionally guarded (DO/EXCEPTION and `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='vector')`) and is a no-op in practice — the live dev DB has no `vector` extension and no `idx_resumes_embedding_hnsw`, and prod runs plain `postgres:15-alpine` which cannot have pgvector. There is therefore NO per-save index-maintenance cost (and embeddings are written only by a targeted UPDATE in embedding_service.py:120-126, not on ordinary resume saves). The genuine issues are: (a) README:13 and README:84 claim DB-side pgvector cosine ranking / an active HNSW index that does not exist — similarity is a Python O(n) `cosine_similarity` loop; (b) dead migration SQL that should be removed or the column migrated to a real `Vector(1536)` type if DB-side search is ever wanted; (c) an unrelated minor cap of `limit(20)` (unordered) in `/ats/semantic-match` that silently omits resumes beyond 20 when no explicit `resume_ids` are supplied.
evidence: 0002 runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` and `CREATE INDEX idx_resumes_embedding_hnsw ON resumes USING hnsw ((content_embedding::vector(1536)) vector_cosine_ops)`. The column is actually `FLOAT[]` (confirmed via \d resumes: `content_embedding | double precision[]`) and the model maps it as `ARRAY(Float)`, not pgvector's Vector type. `rg '<=>|content_embedding' backend/app` finds no query using the `<=>` operator or the indexed cast expression — the only reads are plain Python attribute access. Similarity is computed in Python: `similarity_score = round(max(0.0, self.cosine_similarity(resume_emb, jd_emb)) * 100, 1)` over a hand-rolled `cosine_similarity(a: List[float], b: List[float])`. The endpoint also hard-caps at `select(Resume).where(Resume.user_id == user_id).limit(20)`.
repro: static-only: `rg -n 'content_embedding|<=>' backend/app` returns only Python-side reads plus the model definition; EXPLAIN on the semantic-match query shows a plain scan via idx_resumes_user_id with no vector operator.

title: Snippet install/upvote counters: lost-update race plus unhandled composite-PK IntegrityError → HTTP 500
impact: Two concurrent install/upvote requests from the same user (double-click or retried request) both pass the existence check, both INSERT, and one violates snippet_installs_pkey / snippet_upvotes_pkey — the uncaught IntegrityError surfaces as a 500. Independently, concurrent installs from different users all read the same installs_count and write the same incremented value, so the marketplace counts drift permanently below the true row count (and installs_count is the listing sort key).
fix: Use `insert(SnippetInstall).values(...).on_conflict_do_nothing()` and increment atomically with `update(Snippet).where(Snippet.id==...).values(installs_count=Snippet.installs_count + 1)`, applied only when the insert actually reported a row.
corr: The code pattern is real and both issues are genuine, but severity is low, not medium. (a) The same-user duplicate INSERT window is a few milliseconds wide and the composite PK plus full transaction rollback (get_db rolls back, app/core/errors.py catch-all returns 500) means no duplicate row and no counter corruption — the observable impact is a spurious 500 log entry and a "Failed to install snippet" toast while the winning request already succeeded. (b) The read-modify-write lost update on installs_count/upvotes_count is real under READ COMMITTED and is not self-healing (no reconciliation job), but it only triggers on truly concurrent writes to the same snippet row and results in cosmetic under-counting that skews the 'popular'/'official' sort slightly; uninstall's max(0, ...) clamp prevents negative values. Fix is one statement per endpoint: insert(...).on_conflict_do_nothing() and a SQL-side increment (installs_count=Snippet.installs_count + 1) gated on rowcount.
evidence: install_snippet does check-then-act: `existing = await db.execute(select(SnippetInstall).where(SnippetInstall.snippet_id == snippet_id, SnippetInstall.user_id == user_id))` then `if existing.scalar_one_or_none() is None: db.add(SnippetInstall(...)); snippet.installs_count = (snippet.installs_count or 0) + 1; await db.commit()`. There is no try/except around the commit and no INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. toggle_upvote uses the identical read-modify-write on `snippet.upvotes_count`.
repro: Fire two simultaneous `POST /snippets/{id}/install` for the same snippet+user → one returns 500 (IntegrityError on the composite PK). Fire N concurrent installs from N users → installs_count < `SELECT count(*) FROM snippet_installs WHERE snippet_id=...`.

title: Next.js middleware hard-codes the production hostname allowlist, so any other deployment domain triggers a blocking backend fetch on every request
impact: On a staging domain, a preview URL, an IP address, or any non-`latexy.io` production hostname, every page load and every auth/API request pays an extra uncached round-trip to FastAPI, and a slow or down backend becomes site-wide latency. On any host outside that literal set — in practice Vercel preview deployments, since frontend/vercel.json deploys to Vercel — every request awaits an uncached fetch to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/portfolio/resolve-domain`. The fetch has no AbortSignal.timeout, so an unresponsive backend stalls every request; errors are otherwise caught and pass through, so the failure mode is added latency rather than an outage. title: Deleting all editor content unmounts Monaco and leaves editorRef pointing at a disposed editor
impact: Clearing the document ejects the user out of the editor into a placeholder screen — they cannot simply keep typing and must click "Insert Sample Resume". Meanwhile `handleSave`/`runCompile` read `editorRef.current?.getValue() || latexContent` against a disposed Monaco instance, so the values they persist/compile are no longer trustworthy.

title: WYSIWYG mode is persisted to localStorage but the parsed document is not, leaving the editor stuck on "Parsing…" after reload

Parsing…
: …`.

title: A previously-rendered PDF is destroyed as soon as a new job starts, so a failed compile leaves the user with no preview
impact: Starting an AI optimization or a recompile immediately revokes the blob URL of the working PDF. If the new job fails (a LaTeX error is the common case), `pdfUrl` is null and `PDFPreview` falls back to "No preview yet — Compile your LaTeX to see the PDF". The user loses their last good render and any SyncTeX mapping, and must fix the error blind.
fix: Keep the previous blob URL and render it dimmed with a "stale" badge while a job runs; only revoke it once a new PDF has been downloaded (the success branch at line 1117 already does exactly that).
corr: Real but low severity, and it is a UX regression rather than data loss. The effect at frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:1125-1134 revokes the current PDF blob URL and clears activePdfJobId the moment a compile or AI job enters queued/processing. During the run the loss is hidden by PDFPreview's "Compiling…" spinner, but if the job ends in `failed` the preview pane falls back to "No preview yet", SyncTeX mapping is lost, and the Download PDF / watermark buttons vanish (all gated on pdfUrl). Nothing is destroyed server-side — the LaTeX source is intact, the compiler error log is still shown, and a successful recompile restores the preview — so the user is inconvenienced (no reference render while fixing errors) rather than blocked. Fix: keep the existing blob until either a replacement PDF is downloaded or the job actually fails, i.e. drop the eager revoke on `anyRunning` and rely on the already-correct revoke-after-download at line 1117 (optionally dimming the stale preview to signal it is out of date).
evidence:
```
const anyRunning = compileStream.status === 'queued' || … aiStream.status === 'processing'
if (anyRunning && pdfUrlRef.current) {
  URL.revokeObjectURL(pdfUrlRef.current)
  pdfUrlRef.current = null
  setPdfUrl(null)
  activePdfJobId.current = null
}
```
repro: Compile successfully, then introduce a LaTeX syntax error and compile again. The preview goes from a rendered PDF to "No preview yet".

title: Two download paths revoke the blob URL synchronously after click, contradicting the fix already applied in ExportDropdown
impact: Bulk resume export (.zip) and the editor's PDF download can produce a failed/empty download: the object URL is revoked in the same tick the browser is asked to fetch it. The un-appended anchor makes `click()` a no-op in some browsers as well. The user sees a "Download started" toast and no file.
fix: Reuse the `downloadBlob` helper pattern from ExportDropdown.tsx (append to body, click, remove, `setTimeout(revoke, 1000)`) in both call sites.
corr: Six download call sites revoke the object URL synchronously after `a.click()` instead of using the delayed-revocation helper pattern documented in ExportDropdown.tsx:44-54 — workspace/page.tsx:204, workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:1509, workspace/[resumeId]/cover-letter/page.tsx:656, workspace/[resumeId]/optimize/page.tsx:795, components/WatermarkDownloadPopover.tsx:56, components/GenerateReferencesModal.tsx:83. This is a low-severity robustness/duplication issue, not a reproducible broken download: current browsers retain a blob reference from the click dispatch, and the detached anchor is not itself a problem. The real defect is six copies of ad-hoc blob-download logic that should all call the single `downloadBlob` helper; extract it to a shared util. The claimed symptom of a "Download started" toast with no file applies only to the bulk-export path (the edit page shows no success toast), and has not been demonstrated to occur.
evidence: ExportDropdown does it correctly and documents why: `document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); document.body.removeChild(a); // Delay revocation to ensure the download has started\n setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000)`. The bulk export in workspace/page.tsx and the PDF download in the edit page instead do `a.href = url; a.download = …; a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` with no delay and without appending the anchor to the document.
repro: Click "Export all" on /workspace, or the PDF download button in the editor, on a browser that resolves the blob fetch asynchronously.

title: Reconnect resubscribes without last_event_id whenever no event was received on the previous connection, dropping the entire outage window
impact: If the socket drops between subscribing and the first event (exactly the window where a queued job is waiting for a worker), the resubscribe asks for live-only delivery and every event produced during the disconnect — potentially including the terminal event — is never delivered nor replayable. This directly contradicts the file's own header: 'Auto-resubscribes all pending jobs on reconnect, sending last_event_id so the server replays missed events.'
fix: Default the stored cursor to `'0'` instead of `undefined` when subscribing, so a reconnect always replays from the last known position or from the start of the stream.
corr: The defect is real but should be restated: WSClient never supplies a default replay position, so any subscribe that has not yet observed a stream_id (both the initial `wsClient.subscribe(jobId)` in useJobStream.ts:47 and the onopen resubscribe) asks the server for live-only delivery, and backend/app/core/event_bus.py:98-102 skips replay entirely. Events persisted in latexy:stream:{job_id} during the gap — potentially including the terminal event — are never delivered, and useJobStatus's REST poll cannot recover it because it is gated on status queued/processing while status is still 'idle'. Fix is a one-liner: store `lastEventId ?? '0'` (or send last_event_id: '0' when unknown). Severity is closer to low-medium than medium, since reconnect backoff starts at 100ms and it requires a long-lived disconnect that lands before the first event.
evidence: `subscribe(jobId, lastEventId)` stores `undefined` (`this._subscriptions.set(jobId, lastEventId)`), and the stored value is only upgraded inside `_handleMessage` when an event actually arrives (`this._subscriptions.set(jobId, streamId)`). `onopen` then does `for (const [jobId, lastEventId] of this._subscriptions) this._sendSubscribe(jobId, lastEventId)` and `_sendSubscribe` omits the field when falsy: `if (lastEventId) msg.last_event_id = lastEventId`.
repro: Subscribe to a queued job, kill the WS (restart the backend) before the worker publishes anything, let the client reconnect: the server sends no replay and the UI never advances.

title: useJobStatus's advertised 'REST polling fallback' can never bootstrap state and re-fires onComplete every 5 seconds
impact: The documented fallback for 'when WS is unavailable' does nothing when WS delivers nothing (status stays `idle`, so polling never even starts). When it does run, `isLoading` stays true and `isComplete`/`result` stay false forever while the consumer's onComplete callback fires repeatedly — in JobQueue.tsx:110 that means `onJobComplete` re-fires every 5 seconds for the lifetime of the component.
fix: Expose an `applySnapshot` action on useJobStream's reducer (mapping the REST snapshot's status/percent/stage into state) and dispatch it from refresh; also allow polling to start from `idle` so it can bootstrap when WS events were missed, and guard onComplete with a ref so it fires once.
corr: The finding is correct except for one overstatement: it is not true that "state.status can never transition" — it transitions normally via WebSocket events, and a terminal WS event does clear the interval. The defect is precisely: (a) the REST snapshot is never written into the useJobStream reducer, so polling can neither bootstrap state from `idle` (meaning the advertised "WS unavailable" fallback is a no-op) nor terminate the loop; and (b) in the partial-failure case where WS delivers `queued`/`processing` and then goes silent, the 5s interval keeps running and `onComplete` re-fires on every tick while `isLoading` stays true and `isComplete`/`result` stay false. Severity medium is fair given user-visible repeat toasts in useATSScoring and repeated `onJobComplete` in JobQueue, but note the repeat requires a mid-stream WS drop rather than occurring on every normal run.
evidence: `refresh()` fetches `apiClient.getJobState(jobId)` but never dispatches into the useJobStream reducer — it only invokes callback refs. It also bails unless the stream is already active (`if (state.status !== 'queued' && state.status !== 'processing') return`), and the polling effect has the same precondition (`if (!jobId || (state.status !== 'queued' && state.status !== 'processing')) return`). Because nothing writes the snapshot into state, `state.status` can never transition, so the 5s interval never stops and `onCompleteRef.current(...)` is called on every tick once the snapshot reads `completed`.
repro: Static-only: trace `refresh()` — it has no `dispatch` and no `setState` that affects `state.status`.

title: job.retrying is published by workers but is unhandled everywhere on the frontend, freezing the UI silently for up to 10 minutes
impact: When a compile or LLM task fails transiently, the progress bar sticks at whatever percent it last reached for up to 600 seconds with no message, no attempt counter, and no error — indistinguishable from a hung job. The comment in latex_worker says the intent was to 'surface a transient retrying event', which is not implemented on the consumer side.
fix: Add a `job.retrying` case to the reducer (set status 'processing', message `Retrying (attempt N)…`, reset percent) plus the matching TS type and a `_STATUS_MAP` entry.
corr: Workers emit `job.retrying` (latex_worker.py:194,551; orchestrator.py:125,300) but no consumer handles it: absent from the frontend `AnyEvent` union (event-types.ts) and swallowed by the reducer's `default: return state` (useJobStream.reducer.ts:202), and absent from the backend typed union in backend/app/models/event_schemas.py (not app/schemas/). The effect is cosmetic, not a hang: the UI retains status `processing` with the last percent/message during backoff - deliberate per the worker comments - and resumes updating when the retry runs (job.retrying then job.progress 5%); a terminal job.failed is still published once retries are exhausted. The stale window is at most 240s for LaTeX compiles (max_retries=3 -> 60/120/240s) and 60s for the orchestrator (max_retries=1), not 600s; the 600s cap in the countdown expression is unreachable. The path only triggers on unexpected exceptions - compile errors, validation failures, and compile timeouts all take terminal job.failed branches. The missing piece is only the user-facing "retrying, attempt N" indication plus the typed schema. Severity: low.
evidence: Workers deliberately emit `publish_event(job_id, "job.retrying", {..., "attempt": ...})` instead of job.failed before `raise self.retry(countdown=min(60 * (2 ** self.request.retries), 600), exc=exc)`. The frontend `AnyEvent` union has no `job.retrying` member and the reducer's `default: return state` swallows it; `event_schemas.py` also has no JobRetryingEvent and `_STATUS_MAP` has no entry for it.
repro: Force a transient worker exception (e.g. Redis blip during compile) and observe the client state is unchanged by the job.retrying event.

title: Collab WebSocket accepts legacy HS256 JWTs even when the legacy auth path is disabled
impact: Any holder of a legacy token (including one already revoked/rotated out of the session table) can authenticate to /ws/collab/{resume_id} and, if listed as owner/collaborator by that user id, read and mutate the Y.js document — an auth surface the operator believes is disabled.
fix: Replace the direct `auth_middleware.user_id(token)` call with the same gated helper used by REST (respect `settings.LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED`), or drop the fallback entirely.
corr: Real but lower severity (low-medium, not medium): collab_websocket (backend/app/api/ws_routes.py:274) is the only call site that invokes the legacy HS256 decoder without the settings.LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED gate applied on the REST path, so the WS surface ignores the operator's "legacy auth off" setting. However, no code in the repo issues legacy JWTs any more, the decoder requires a non-expired `exp`, and the subsequent owner/collaborator lookup means the token subject must already be a real owner or collaborator. So this is a feature-flag/defense-in-depth bypass exploitable only by someone holding an unexpired legacy token or knowing JWT_SECRET_KEY, not a general unauthenticated access path. Fix: wrap the fallback in the same LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED check or remove it.
evidence: `collab_websocket` does `user_id = await _validate_better_auth_session(token, db)` and then `if not user_id: user_id = auth_middleware.user_id(token)`. `auth_middleware` is `_jwt_validator = _LegacyJWTValidator(...)`, i.e. the raw legacy decoder. The REST path deliberately gates that decoder: 'Legacy JWT fallback — OFF by default ... if getattr(settings, "LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED", False)'. The WS path skips the flag entirely and also never checks that the JWT subject corresponds to an existing, non-revoked user.
repro: Static-only: mint an HS256 token with `sub` set to a user id using JWT_SECRET_KEY while LEGACY_JWT_ENABLED=false and connect to /ws/collab/<their-resume-id>.

title: Public portfolio page exposes the titles of every non-archived resume, not just public ones
impact: Enabling a public portfolio publishes the title of every resume the user owns, including private per-company variants. Batch-tailor auto-names forks `"{parent.title} — {company_name}"` (job_routes.py:578), so an unauthenticated visitor to /u/<username> can enumerate exactly which companies the user is applying to.
fix: Add an explicit per-resume publish flag (or reuse `share_token IS NOT NULL`) and filter on it in `get_portfolio`; default to publishing nothing.

Precise version: the unauthenticated `GET /portfolio/{username}` endpoint (backend/app/api/portfolio_routes.py:257-292) returns id/title/created_at/updated_at for every non-archived resume owned by a user who has opted into `portfolio_enabled`, despite the docstring, the `PublicResumeOut` model name, and the frontend's "No public resumes yet" copy all implying a public subset. Because no per-resume visibility column exists on `Resume` (only the unrelated opt-in `share_token`), there is no way for a user to keep an individual resume off their portfolio short of archiving it, so batch-tailor fork titles of the form `"{parent.title} — {company_name}"` (job_routes.py:580) are disclosed to anonymous visitors. Fix requires adding a per-resume visibility/portfolio-inclusion column and filtering on it (defaulting to excluded).
evidence:
`get_portfolio` selects `select(Resume).where(Resume.user_id == user.id, Resume.archived_at.is_(None))` — the only gate is `user.portfolio_enabled`. There is no per-resume visibility column: `grep -n 'is_public|visibility' backend/app/database/models.py` returns nothing; the only sharing mechanism on `Resume` is the opt-in `share_token` (models.py:192-194), which this query ignores. `/u/[username]/page.tsx` renders `resumes.map(r =>

{r.title}

)` for every returned row, and the endpoint requires no auth.

title: dropbox_sync_enabled is missing from the backend ResumeResponse, so the editor's Dropbox toggle always shows "off"
impact: After any reload of the editor, Dropbox sync appears disabled even when it is enabled in the DB: the button tooltip says "Enable Dropbox sync", the push-to-Dropbox control (`{dbxSyncEnabled && ...}`) is hidden, and clicking the toggle re-runs `enableDropboxSync` (a full initial push) instead of disabling.

But the Pydantic `ResumeResponse` only declares the GitHub trio (`github_sync_enabled`, `github_repo_name`, `github_last_sync_at`) — `grep -n dropbox backend/app/api/resume_routes.py` returns nothing, so `GET /resumes/{id}` never serialises the field. title: middleware.ts provides no auth gating and runs a blocking backend fetch on every request for any host not named latexy.io
impact: (a) On any deployment whose hostname isn't literally latexy.io — e.g. the `your-app.vercel.app` / `your-domain.com` hosts in .env.production.example and .env.production, or every preview deployment — every single request (page loads, Better Auth `/api/auth/*` calls, public assets) pays an extra uncached round-trip + DB query, and a backend outage stalls the whole site. (b) Because no route is gated here, protection depends entirely on per-page client redirects, which the five pages in the infinite-spinner finding omit.
fix: Drive the known-host list from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`/an env var instead of hardcoding, narrow the matcher to exclude `/api`, `/_next` and static assets, cache resolve-domain results, and add an explicit session-cookie check for the private route prefixes.
corr: Low severity, and only the performance/robustness half stands. Correct claim: frontend/src/middleware.ts resolves custom portfolio domains with an uncached (`cache:'no-store'`), un-timed-out awaited fetch to `/portfolio/resolve-domain` (a DB SELECT, backend/app/api/portfolio_routes.py:235) on every non-allowlisted-host request, and the matcher `'/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'` is broader than needed (it also covers /api/auth/* and files in /public). Fixes: add an AbortController timeout, cache the domain→username mapping (Next.js `revalidate` or Redis), and tighten the matcher. Scope corrections: latexy.io / www.latexy.io / localhost / 127.0.0.1 and any /u/* path short-circuit at lines 30-37, so production apex traffic is unaffected; the affected hosts are real custom domains (where a lookup is inherent to the feature) and preview deployments. The "backend outage stalls the whole site" claim is wrong — errors are caught and pass through (lines 54-56); only a hanging (not failing) backend would stall. The "no auth gating" claim is not a defect: authorization is enforced server-side in FastAPI (`get_current_user` on 239 endpoints), Next pages are client-rendered shells with no sensitive server-rendered data, and most protected pages already redirect client-side.
evidence: `LATEXY_DOMAINS = new Set(['latexy.io','www.latexy.io','localhost','127.0.0.1'])`. For any other hostname the middleware performs `await fetch(`${apiBase}/portfolio/resolve-domain?domain=...`, {cache:'no-store'})` — a DB query (`portfolio_routes.py:235`) — before the request proceeds. The matcher is `'/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'`, i.e. it also matches `/api/auth/*` and everything in /public. There is no session check anywhere in the file, so no route is protected server-side; the comment block only describes portfolio domain routing.
repro: Static: set the deployment host to anything outside the hardcoded set and observe one `/portfolio/resolve-domain` call per request in backend logs.

title: k8s image names do not match anything the build pipeline produces (celery/beat/flower use latexy-backend:latest, app pods use ghcr.io/your-org/...)
loc: k8s/celery/celery-worker.yaml (image: latexy-backend:latest, three deployments), k8s/backend/deployment.yaml (image: ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-backend:latest), k8s/frontend/deployment.yaml (ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-frontend:latest), .github/workflows/release.yml, Makefile build-backend/build-frontend
impact: `make build` fails outright on the frontend target; a k8s apply leaves celery-worker/celery-beat/flower in ImagePullBackOff (nothing publishes latexy-backend:latest) and backend/frontend in ImagePullBackOff against the placeholder org — so no async job ever runs.
fix: Point Makefile build-frontend at frontend/Dockerfile.prod, use one image reference (ghcr.io/<owner>/latexy-backend) across all k8s deployments, and template the org/tag instead of hardcoding your-org/latest.
corr: Two narrower defects, severity low: (1) `make build-frontend` (Makefile:203-205) fails because it passes `-f frontend/Dockerfile`, which does not exist (only frontend/Dockerfile.dev and frontend/Dockerfile.prod); the Makefile help text at lines 70-71 also advertises tags that differ from what the recipes build. (2) k8s/celery/celery-worker.yaml:22,121,183 use the bare name `latexy-backend:latest` with no imagePullPolicy, while k8s/backend/deployment.yaml:22 and k8s/frontend/deployment.yaml:22 use `ghcr.io/your-org/...`; since `your-org` is an intentional placeholder (matching k8s/namespace.yaml:50) but `latexy-backend:latest` is not marked as one, an operator who correctly substitutes the org still leaves worker/beat/flower pointing at an image release.yml never publishes. Not part of the claim: the `eyJhdXRocyI6e319` registry-secret is a documented placeholder and does not block anonymous pulls of public GHCR images, and nothing in CI/CD or documentation invokes k8s/deploy.sh, so no currently active deployment path is broken.
evidence: release.yml pushes `ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/latexy-backend` / `-frontend`. The Makefile builds `ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-backend:latest` and `ghcr.io/your-org/latexy-frontend:latest` — and `build-frontend` uses `-f frontend/Dockerfile`, a file that does not exist (only Dockerfile.dev and Dockerfile.prod are present). The celery worker/beat/flower deployments reference the bare local name `latexy-backend:latest` with `imagePullSecrets: registry-secret` whose data is `eyJhdXRocyI6e319` (empty auths).
repro: make build → "unable to prepare context: ... frontend/Dockerfile: no such file or directory"; kubectl apply -f k8s/celery/celery-worker.yaml → ImagePullBackOff.

title: scripts/deploy/deploy.sh cannot succeed: tags images that compose never creates and health-checks an unpublished port
impact: The documented production deploy path fails every time — first at image tagging, and if that is patched, five minutes later with a false 'Some services are not healthy' failure.
fix: Add explicit `image:` names to docker-compose.prod.yml services (also needed for the documented `docker compose pull`), and health-check through nginx (`curl -f http://localhost/health`) or `docker compose exec backend curl localhost:8030/health`.
corr: Downgrade to low severity and narrow the claim: in `scripts/deploy/deploy.sh`, `check_service_health()` (lines 254-286) polls `http://localhost:8000/health` while `docker-compose.prod.yml` publishes no host port for `backend` (only nginx 80/443, flower, prometheus, alertmanager, tempo, grafana), so the check burns 300s and makes `deploy_services` return 1 -> `main` exits 1 after containers are up but before migrations. Fix by exec'ing the healthcheck inside the container or probing nginx (`http://localhost/api/health`). The image-tagging claim is incorrect: Compose builds `latexy-frontend`/`latexy-backend` in the canonical `Latexy` checkout (project name = lowercased dir), so the tags usually match; and because `build_images` is called as `if ! build_images`, `set -e` is suppressed in its body, so a failing `docker tag` would neither abort nor fail the function. Finally, this script is unreferenced dead code — the documented deploy path is `k8s/deploy.sh` via `make k8s-deploy` — so real-world impact is near zero.
evidence: deploy.sh runs with `set -euo pipefail`, then after building via `docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml build` it executes `docker tag latexy-frontend:latest "latexy-frontend:$version"` and `docker tag latexy-backend:latest ...` — compose builds images named <project>-backend/<project>-frontend, so those tags do not exist and docker tag exits non-zero, aborting the script. If it got further, `check_service_health()` polls `http://localhost:8000/health` 30 times × 10s, but docker-compose.prod.yml publishes no host port for backend (only nginx 80/443, flower 5555, prometheus, grafana), so it always times out and deploy_services returns 1.
repro: DEPLOY_ENV=production bash scripts/deploy/deploy.sh → aborts at `docker tag latexy-backend:latest`.

title: Release notes tell operators to `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml pull`, but that file has no image: keys — the published GHCR images are never used
loc: .github/workflows/release.yml (Deploy section of the release body), docker-compose.prod.yml:25-176
impact: Operators following the release instructions silently deploy a local rebuild of whatever the working tree contains, not the tagged image the pipeline published — release immutability is lost.
fix: Add `image: ghcr.io/<owner>/latexy-backend:${VERSION:-latest}` (and frontend) alongside build: in docker-compose.prod.yml so pull/up use the released tags.
corr: Low severity, scoped as a release-process/docs inconsistency: the release body generated in .github/workflows/release.yml (lines 147-156) tells operators to `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml pull && up -d`, but docker-compose.prod.yml's five app services (frontend L25, backend L52, celery-worker L98, celery-beat L142, flower L172) declare only `build:` and no `image:`, so the GHCR images published by the build-backend/build-frontend jobs are never consumed by the documented deploy path. `pull` still succeeds (it pulls nginx/redis/postgres/monitoring images and only warns about build-only services) and `up -d` builds the app services from the tagged checkout — so the deployed *source* still matches the release; what is lost is use of the tested prebuilt artifact and its CI build-args (BUILD_VERSION, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api), not release source fidelity. Note scripts/deploy/deploy.sh treats build-from-source as the intended prod flow (its `pull` at L230 is commented "if using registry"), so the fix is either to add `image: ghcr.io/<owner>/latexy-{backend,frontend}:${TAG}` alongside `build:` in docker-compose.prod.yml, or to correct the release notes to instruct a build rather than a pull.
evidence: release.yml's release body says: "# Pull new images / docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml pull / docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d". Every service in docker-compose.prod.yml specifies only `build: {context, dockerfile}` and no `image:`, so compose has nothing to pull and `up -d` rebuilds locally from the checkout instead of running the released, tested artifact.
repro: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml pull → nothing to pull for build-only services.

title: Makefile dev/test targets reference a different compose file than the test helpers require, so `make infra && make test-backend` cannot work
impact: Following the Makefile help text ("test-backend  pytest backend/test/ (local DB — requires make infra)") always fails with "ERROR: latexy-postgres container is not running. Run: make infra"; `make logs-backend` errors with 'no such service: backend'. Contributors must know the undocumented scripts/dev.sh path instead.
fix: Point COMPOSE_FILE/infra at docker-compose.yml (the file that defines latexy-postgres on 5434), or align backend/docker-compose.yml's container name/port and service names — and fix logs-backend's service name.
corr: Real but low severity (dev tooling only, documented workaround exists). Corrected claim: the Makefile's `COMPOSE_FILE := backend/docker-compose.yml` is out of sync with the rest of the Makefile, which assumes the root `docker-compose.yml`. Two concrete defects: (1) `make infra` brings up backend/docker-compose.yml, whose postgres is `latexy-postgres-dev` on host port 5432 with user `${DB_USER:-postgres}` and a mandatory `${DB_PASSWORD:?...}` (no backend/.env exists, so it errors immediately), while `test-db-setup`/`test-backend` require a running container literally named `latexy-postgres` reachable at localhost:5434 as user `latexy` — i.e. the root compose's postgres. The help text "test-backend ... requires make infra" is therefore wrong. (2) `make logs-backend` runs `docker compose -f backend/docker-compose.yml logs -f backend`, but that file's API service is named `latexy-backend`, so it fails with "no such service: backend". Impact is narrower than claimed: `make run` (root compose, the first documented command in README) and the documented `./scripts/dev.sh infra` both create `latexy-postgres` on 5434, so `make test-backend` does work via those paths — the fix is to point `infra`/`down`/`logs*` at `$(ROOT_COMPOSE)` (or its infra services) and correct the service name/help text.
evidence: Makefile: `COMPOSE_FILE := backend/docker-compose.yml` and `infra: docker compose -f $(COMPOSE_FILE) up -d`. backend/docker-compose.yml names its postgres `container_name: latexy-postgres-dev` on host port 5432 and its API service `latexy-backend`. But `test-db-setup` asserts `docker inspect latexy-postgres` and runs `docker exec latexy-postgres psql ...` with LOCAL_TEST_SYNC_URL pointing at localhost:5434 (the root compose port), and `logs-backend` runs `docker compose -f backend/docker-compose.yml logs -f backend` for a service named latexy-backend.
repro: make infra && make test-backend → ERROR: latexy-postgres container is not running.

title: worktree-up.sh starts per-slot Compose projects that re-create the shared infra containers, hitting container-name and host-port conflicts
loc: scripts/worktree-up.sh (start_slot: `docker compose -p "$PROJECT_NAME" up -d backend worker beat frontend flower`), docker-compose.yml:46-56,66-71,127,145-149,236-240
impact: The documented second-clone workflow (`./scripts/worktree-up.sh w2`) fails with 'Conflict. The container name "/latexy-postgres" is already in use' / port-already-allocated, so the multi-slot Docker path only works for slot 1.
fix: Pass `--no-deps` in start_slot (infra readiness is already ensured by ensure_infra), or drop the fixed container_name/host-port bindings from the infra services.
corr: Core defect confirmed, with two refinements: (1) the container-name conflict on latexy-postgres is what actually aborts the run — the fixed host ports (6379, 9000, 5434) are a secondary symptom that would only surface if names were unique; (2) the network is not a problem (networks.default.name: latexy-network is shared, producing only a cosmetic "a network with name latexy-network exists but was not created for project" warning). Impact is limited to the full-Docker multi-slot dev path (./scripts/worktree-up.sh w2/w3/w4); the preferred hybrid path ./scripts/dev.sh app is unaffected, so severity is medium at most (dev-tooling only, no runtime/security impact). Fix: add --no-deps to the per-slot `docker compose up` (safe because ensure_infra already health-gates postgres and redis), or split infra into its own compose file.
evidence: docker-compose.yml's backend declares `depends_on: postgres: {condition: service_healthy}, redis: {condition: service_healthy}` and frontend depends on postgres+backend. `docker compose up -d backend ...` starts depends_on services by default, but postgres/redis/minio use fixed `container_name: latexy-postgres` / `latexy-redis` / `latexy-minio` and fixed host ports (`${DB_PORT:-5434}:5432`, `6379:6379`, `9000:9000`) — the shared infra started under project `latexy` already owns those names and ports.
repro: ./scripts/dev.sh infra (starts project latexy) then ./scripts/worktree-up.sh w2 → container name conflict on latexy-postgres.

title: Compile-settings modal exposes flags and a TeX Live version that the worker silently discards
impact: A user enables "Shell escape (for minted, svg, etc.)" or pins "TeX Live 2022", gets a `toast.success('Compile settings saved')`, and nothing changes — minted/svg documents keep failing with no explanation of why the setting had no effect. (Excluding --shell-escape is the correct security posture; advertising it in the UI is the defect.)
fix: Remove `--shell-escape`, `--synctex=1`, `--interaction=nonstopmode`, `--halt-on-error` and the TeX Live version selector from the modal (or mark them read-only/"always on" / "coming soon"), and have the settings endpoint 400 on flags outside the server whitelist instead of accepting and dropping them.
corr:
Two smaller UI/backend mismatches in the compile-settings modal, severity low (cosmetic/UX, no security or data impact):

1. `texlive_version` is a dead setting. The modal (frontend/src/components/CompileSettingsModal.tsx:22-27) offers 2022/2023/2024; resume_routes.py:181-192/885-886 validates and persists it; job_routes.py:343-347 forwards it in compile_settings — but no worker or service ever reads it. latex_worker.py:278, orchestrator.py:551 and latex_service.py:125/257 always use the hardcoded `LATEX_DOCKER_IMAGE = "texlive/texlive:latest"`. The user sees `toast.success('Compile settings saved')` and nothing changes. Fix: drop the dropdown, or map the value to a versioned image tag.

2. `--shell-escape` is listed as a selectable (non-disabled) checkbox via ALLOWED_LATEXMK_FLAGS in frontend/src/lib/api-client.ts:27-33, but resume_routes.py's own ALLOWED_LATEXMK_FLAGS deliberately excludes it, so PATCH /resumes/{id}/settings returns 422. Impact is not a silent no-op — the modal shows toast.error and the entire save is rejected, so the user also loses their compiler/main_file/package edits in that submit. Fix: remove `--shell-escape` from the frontend list (or mark it unavailable) so the frontend and backend whitelists agree.

The finding's stated impact ("shell escape enabled, success toast, silently discarded by the worker") does not hold; the API rejects it before it can be stored.
evidence: The modal offers five toggles including `'--shell-escape': 'Shell escape (for minted, svg, etc.)'` and a TeX Live version dropdown (2022/2023/2024). The worker filters them down to one: `_ALLOWED_EXTRA_FLAGS = {"--file-line-error"}` and `custom_flags = [f for f in (_cs.get("latexmk_flags") or []) if f in _ALLOWED_EXTRA_FLAGS]`. `texlive_version` is collected into `compile_settings` by job_routes but `grep -n texlive backend/app/workers backend/app/services` only matches `LATEX_DOCKER_IMAGE: str = "texlive/texlive:latest"` — the value is never read anywhere.
repro: Open Compile Settings, tick Shell escape, Save, then compile a document using `\usepackage{minted}`.

title: Export dropdown in the editor exports the last-saved DB copy, not the current buffer; its "PDF" entry is a dead end
impact: A user edits their resume, exports to DOCX/MD/TXT/JSON without saving, and silently receives the previous version — a data-loss-shaped surprise with no warning. Choosing "PDF" from a menu whose own description says "Compiled PDF document" downloads nothing.
fix: Pass `latexContent={currentLatex}` and `onPdfExport={handleDownload}` from the editor, and in `handleExport` prefer the in-editor content (`exportContent`) over `exportResume`, or force a save first.
corr: Low severity, narrower than claimed: in the editor ExportDropdown receives only resumeId, so non-PDF exports (docx/md/txt/json/html/yaml/xml/canva/figma) are generated from the last-saved DB row rather than the live buffer, and since the editor has no autosave an unsaved user silently downloads a stale file. Fix by passing latexContent (or calling updateResume first, matching the existing GitHub/Dropbox push pattern in the same file) and by passing onPdfExport={handleDownload}. The PDF entry is not a broken dead end — it falls back to an explanatory toast, and the editor already exposes a working PDF download button once a compile has produced pdfUrl.
evidence: The editor renders `<ExportDropdown resumeId={resumeId} variant="toolbar" />` — neither `latexContent` nor `onPdfExport` is passed. `handleExport` then takes the `if (resumeId) { blob = await apiClient.exportResume(resumeId, format) }` branch, and `export_resume` serves `_convert_latex(resume.latex_content, fmt)` straight from the DB row. For `format === 'pdf'` with no `onPdfExport` prop the handler just does `toast.info('Use the compile button to generate PDF')` and returns.
repro: Open a saved resume, change a bullet without saving, Export → Word. The .docx contains the old bullet.

title: Image/OCR upload is advertised in the UI but the production image lacks tesseract and poppler
impact: In production, dragging a screenshot/photo of a resume into the import wizard always fails with "File could not be parsed — check the file is not corrupted" (the 422 mapping in useFormatConversion), even though the UI accepted the file type. Scanned-PDF OCR fallback fails the same way, and `_resolve_pdftotext_binary()` finds nothing so ATS text extraction always takes the slower pdfminer path.
fix: Add `tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils` to Dockerfile.prod, or gate the image extensions in `MultiFormatUpload` on a capability flag returned by `GET /formats/supported`.
corr: Core defect confirmed: backend/Dockerfile.prod (used by .github/workflows/release.yml:49 and every backend/worker service in docker-compose.prod.yml) omits tesseract-ocr and poppler-utils while requirements.txt installs pytesseract/pdf2image/Pillow, so the ImportError guard in backend/app/parsers/image_parser.py never fires and every image upload — a file type explicitly advertised in frontend/src/components/MultiFormatUpload.tsx:19 — fails with a 422 rendered as 'File could not be parsed — check the file is not corrupted'. Scanned-PDF OCR fallback (backend/app/parsers/pdf_parser.py:47-48) fails the same way but only for PDFs with an empty text layer. The pdftotext claim should be downgraded to a side note: backend/app/workers/latex_worker.py:95-135 degrades gracefully to pdfminer with a warning log, it is a performance regression rather than a failure. Fix is to add `tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils` to the Dockerfile.prod production-stage apt install, and separately to raise a distinct 'OCR unavailable' error instead of masking a missing-binary error as a corrupt-file 422.
evidence: `ACCEPTED_EXTENSIONS` includes `'jpg','jpeg','png','gif','bmp','tiff','webp'` and `parser_factory` maps `ResumeFormat.IMAGE → ImageParser`. `ImageParser.parse` calls `pytesseract.image_to_string(...)` and `ocr_pdf_bytes` calls `convert_from_bytes(...)` (poppler). `backend/Dockerfile` installs `tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils`; `backend/Dockerfile.prod` installs only the texlive packages plus `curl` — no tesseract, no poppler-utils. Both failures land in `except Exception as e: raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse image: {str(e)}")` → `HTTPException(422)`.
repro: Upload a .png resume against a container built from Dockerfile.prod.

title: Non-resume compiles (TikZ preview, anonymised share) are tagged with `resume_id` and get written into the resume's version history
impact: The resume's auto-save history (capped at 20 entries) gets polluted with a 7-line TikZ standalone snippet and with the PII-redacted variant. A user restoring from Version History can silently replace their resume with a TikZ stub or an anonymised copy, and genuine checkpoints get pruned out to make room.
fix: Add an explicit `skip_auto_save: bool` (or reuse a `metadata` marker like `anonymous_share`/`preview`) to `submit_latex_compilation`, and set it for TikZ previews and the anonymised-share compile; drop `resume_id` from the TikZ submit.
corr: Real defect, but low severity rather than medium. latex_worker.py:483-493 excludes only watermarked compiles when deciding to record an auto-save checkpoint, so the TikZ standalone preview (page.tsx:1402, which passes resume_id) and the anonymous-share redacted compile (resume_routes.py:1753, which passes resume_id and metadata.resume_id) can both land in the resume's auto-save history and be restored from Version History. The pre-existing 5-minute dedup in auto_save_worker._do_auto_save caps this at one polluted entry per 5-minute window and suppresses it entirely when a genuine auto-save happened recently, so the "history filled with junk / genuine checkpoints pruned out" impact does not follow; the concrete risk is a single mislabeled "Auto-save — <time>" entry that silently replaces the resume if restored. The fix is to have these callers opt out (e.g. a skip_auto_save flag or checking metadata submitted_via / anonymous_share) rather than relying on the watermark check.
evidence: `handleTikZPreview` builds a throwaway `\documentclass[border=4pt]{standalone}` document and submits it as `apiClient.compileLatex({ latex_content: standaloneDoc, resume_id: resumeId, compiler })`. The share-anonymisation path does `submit_latex_compilation(latex_content=redacted_latex, ..., resume_id=resume_id, metadata={"anonymous_share": True, "resume_id": resume_id})`. On success the worker runs `_resume_id = resume_id or (metadata or {}).get("resume_id"); if _resume_id and user_id and not watermark: record_auto_save_checkpoint.apply_async(args=[_resume_id, user_id, latex_content])` — it excludes watermarked compiles but nothing else.
repro: Open the TikZ editor in the workspace, hit Preview, then open Version History — an auto-save checkpoint containing only the standalone TikZ document appears.

title: Delimiter state machine never flushes its hold-back buffer, silently dropping the last ~14 characters of LaTeX when the end marker is absent
impact: Whenever the stream ends while still inside the LaTeX block (max_tokens truncation, provider disconnect), the already-truncated document loses another 14 characters, guaranteeing a break mid-command; since `latex_parts` is non-empty the JSON fallback at :472 does not trigger, so this mangled document is compiled and reported to the user as a LaTeX error. Truncated changes JSON silently yields `changes_made: []` (`except Exception: raw_changes = []`), so the "what changed" panel is empty with no explanation.
fix: After the stream loop, if `llm_state == _IN_LATEX` append the remaining `buf` to `latex_parts` (and likewise for `_IN_CHANGES`), and flag the run as truncated because the end delimiter was never seen.
corr:
The defect is real but the framing/trigger is off, and the two hold-back lengths differ.

Verified in /Users/sanskar/dev/Latexy2/backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:
- `_LS/_LE/_CS/_CE` at :55-58; `_LE` = "<<<END_LATEX>>>" (15 chars, hold-back 14), `_CE` = "<<<END_CHANGES>>>" (17 chars, hold-back 16 — not 14).
- `_IN_LATEX` else-branch (:435-442) and `_IN_CHANGES` else-branch (:459-465) both do `safe_len = len(buf) - len(_XE) + 1` and keep the remainder in `buf`.
- The `for chunk in stream:` loop (:395) ends at :463; :467-469 compute `optimized_latex = "".join(latex_parts).strip()` with no post-loop flush of `buf`. So the residual tail is genuinely discarded.
- Path is live: `_run_llm_stage` is called from `optimize_and_compile_task` at :136, and the JSON fallback at :472 is gated on `if not optimized_latex`, so it will not rescue a partially-flushed document.

Corrections to the claim:
1. The claimed trigger (max_tokens truncation / disconnect) is the least interesting case: the document is already truncated mid-command, so losing 14 more characters does not change the outcome — compilation fails either way. Impact there is cosmetic.
2. The realistic, user-visible trigger the finding does not state is the LLM emitting a COMPLETE document but omitting the closing `<<<END_LATEX>>>` marker (a common LLM behavior; the prompt at backend/app/services/llm_service.py:352-357 only instructs the format). In that case the last 14 characters of a valid document are dropped — and `\end{document}` is exactly 14 characters, so the result is an otherwise-valid resume that fails to compile with a "missing \end{document}" error, with no fallback triggered.
3. The `changes_made: []` consequence is accurate but is the same omitted/truncated-marker case, and loses 16 chars, not 14.

Fix: after the streaming loop, flush the residual buffer for the current state (`if llm_state == _IN_LATEX and buf: latex_parts.append(buf)`, likewise for `_IN_CHANGES`). Severity low-to-medium (correctness bug, no data loss beyond a failed job the user can retry).
evidence: In `_IN_LATEX` with no `<<<END_LATEX>>>` in the buffer: `safe_len = len(buf) - len(_LE) + 1; if safe_len > 0: latex_parts.append(buf[:safe_len]); buf = buf[safe_len:]` — i.e. the trailing `len(_LE)-1 == 14` characters are deliberately withheld to catch a split delimiter. After the `for chunk in stream` loop ends there is no final flush: `optimized_latex = "".join(latex_parts).strip()` uses only what was flushed, and `buf` is discarded. The identical pattern in `_IN_CHANGES` discards the tail of the changes JSON.
repro: static-only (or set OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS=200 and run a combined job): the final ≤14 chars streamed inside the LaTeX block never reach latex_parts.

title: Every AI endpoint maps provider errors and rate-limit exhaustion to HTTP 200 with echoed-back input, so the UI shows a fake success
impact: When the OpenAI key is invalid, the provider 429/500s, or the caller has burned its 20 platform-key calls/minute, the user sees a normal result panel whose "Rewritten" text is identical to the original, plus an Accept button — indistinguishable from "the AI decided no change was needed". Salary estimates come back as 0/0/0 and section reordering silently returns the current order. No error surfaces to the client, and no upsell/retry hint is possible.
fix: Return a distinct status (502/429 with a machine-readable code, or a `success:false`/`error` field) for provider failures and for the rate-limit path, and have the widgets render the error state they already have instead of the result state.
corr: Scope is one endpoint, not all AI endpoints, and severity is low. Only POST /api/v1/ai/rewrite produces an indistinguishable fake success: on provider exception, empty completion, or `_resolve_ai_api_key` returning None (platform-key limit of 20/min exhausted), backend/app/api/ai_routes.py:497-499 and 530-532 return HTTP 200 with `rewritten = request.selected_text`, and RewriteResponse carries no degraded/error flag; frontend/src/components/WritingAssistantWidget.tsx:79-90 then enters phase 'result' and renders an Original-vs-Rewritten diff with an Accept button for identical text. Fix = add a flag (or non-200) to RewriteResponse, or have the widget short-circuit when `res.rewritten === selectedText`. The other cited endpoints already surface the degradation to the user: bullets (BulletGeneratorWidget.tsx:176-180) and summary (SummaryGeneratorWidget.tsx:151-156) show explicit "check your API key" errors on empty arrays; salary has a dedicated `median === 0` branch showing the backend disclaimer (SalaryEstimatorPanel.tsx:241-246); reorder surfaces "AI suggestion unavailable / no API key configured" through the displayed `rationale` (SectionReorderPanel.tsx:306).
evidence: `except Exception as exc: logger.error(f"rewrite error: {exc}"); return RewriteResponse(rewritten=request.selected_text, action=request.action, cached=False)` — and the same shape when `_resolve_ai_api_key` returns None because `_system_key_rate_limited` tripped. The widget has no way to tell: `const res = await apiClient.rewriteText(...); setRewritten(res.rewritten); setPhase('result')` then renders an "Original" (struck through) vs "Rewritten" diff and an Accept button.
repro: Set OPENAI_API_KEY to an invalid value and POST /ai/rewrite → 200 {"rewritten": <input>, "cached": false}; the widget shows an identical-diff result panel.

title: Anthropic and OpenRouter BYOK keys can be stored and validated but are consumed by nothing; Gemini is advertised and unimplemented
impact: A user who adds an Anthropic or OpenRouter key sees it validated and listed as active and is told it will skip usage limits, yet no resume optimization, cover letter, summary, rewrite or translation will ever use it. A user following the help text and choosing Google/Gemini gets `success:false "Unsupported provider: gemini"` from POST /byok/api-keys and 404 from /byok/models/gemini.
fix: Either route feature calls through `multi_provider_service` using the user's preferred provider, or restrict the BYOK UI/API to `openai` and remove the Gemini enum/mask/help-text claims until a GeminiProvider exists.
corr: Anthropic and OpenRouter BYOK keys can be added, validated, stored and listed as active, and ProviderSelector.tsx:196-205 tells the user they "skip usage limits", but no product feature ever consumes them: resume optimization, ATS, cover letter, summary/rewrite and translation all hardcode api_key_service.get_user_provider(db, user_id, "openai") (ai_routes.py:89, ai_routes.py:1341, ats_routes.py:737, cover_letter_routes.py:300, format_routes.py:423). Non-OpenAI keys are only usable via the generic passthrough POST /byok/generate, which has no frontend caller. Fix is either to make the AI paths provider-aware or to stop offering/promising the other providers. The Gemini portion of the finding does NOT hold: gemini is filtered out of get_supported_providers() by the `in self.provider_classes` check, so it is never offered in the UI, and add_api_key / /byok/models/{provider} reject it with explicit, correct guards. The only Gemini-related issues are cosmetic dead code (the "gemini" entry in mask_api_key at api_key_service.py:334, the unused LLMProvider.GEMINI enum member) and one stale FAQ sentence mentioning Google at HelpCenter.tsx:123. Severity: low-to-medium, not medium-plus — misleading UI and an unused feature, with no security, data or cost impact.
evidence: `provider_classes = {OPENAI: OpenAIProvider, ANTHROPIC: AnthropicProvider, OPENROUTER: OpenRouterProvider}` — no Gemini class, although `LLMProvider.GEMINI = "gemini"` exists and `mask_api_key` has a `"gemini": "AI...****"` entry, and HelpCenter tells users "BYOK … providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google". The only consumer of a non-OpenAI provider anywhere in the codebase is the generic passthrough `POST /byok/generate` (grep: `multi_provider_service.generate` has exactly one caller). Every product feature resolves OpenAI only — `api_key_service.get_user_provider(db, user_id, "openai")` is hardcoded in ai_routes.py:89, ai_routes.py:1341, cover_letter_routes.py:300, format_routes.py:423 — while ProviderSelector renders "Add your own {provider} key above to skip usage limits." for each of the three providers.
